comment: Lectures were helpful, not too much work outside of the projects. However she messed up my grade on a project, when I talked to her about it in class she said to email her about it. She never responded to my email or changed my grade which caused me to get a B instead of B+.

Be prepared for a flipped classroom. Class time is mainly used for "peer instruction" quizzes, which are participation-based, while you're expected to watch lesson materials on Canvas. This approach might feel like the instructor is disengaged, as there's little effort to lecture on relevant material or provide deeper in-class instruction. AVOID!

She does not taking extenuating circumstances into consideration. She unfairly listens to other people in terms of grade curves, but probably won't curve your grade. The tests are extremely easy, but the projects are extremely hard. She responds to your emails during vacation, but she does not take grade boosts into account at all.

She did not teach anything in class. Going to class was a waste of time. She could barely answer questions too. She only assigned online content pages which were helpful if u can teach yourself well. Projects were hard and took a long time. She was not understanding to external circumstances either. I would not recommend her as a teacher.
easy class, you learn most of the material by yourself through the stuff in canvas.

Class is pointless. Only went for participation points. She teaches thru videos in content pages that don't help anyone understand the material. You basically are teaching yourself the rest of the basic concepts of Java continued from CS 1114 from material in Canvas. Prepare to constantly be at office hrs in Torg. She's very condescending too.

Margaret Ellis does NOT care about you, or your problems. I have reached out multiple times for assistance, only to be ignored or, on the rare instance of being acklowdged, have my problems be completely disregarded. This has been going on since the beginning of the semester.

The lectures are practically not useful for your time, but her online content pages are very helpful and teach you for most of the semester. The class is easy, and if you need further help, the TA's are helpful as well. Just don't procrastinate!

Her and a lot of the TAs (but definitely not all of them) are really rude. All content is taught through online videos and the lecture is treated like a study hall that no one attends. Fortunately, it is a really easy class content-wise, with test questions repeated from earlier quizzes and free hundreds from projects if you start them in time.

Professor Ellis is amazing! The class is very easy if you just start your projects early and study for the quizzes by reviewing past quizzes and questions on the content pages. The assesments are literally mostly just repeated questions from the previous quizzes. You don't really have to go to her class to do well, but I recommend still going.

Welcome to Yappsville! Prof. Ellis is the mayor. Lectures are completely useless, she isn't good at actually teaching, and can be rude/delusional. Content/class isn't hard, just prepare to learn most of it through youtube and other online tutorials. TAs are great and can absolutely help, so go to office hours. Dont waste your time going to class.
I really really dont like her.
bruh all she does is yap yap yap and there is nothing helpful. there's so much work ive never ever had so much homework its not even funny.

I've went to like 7 of her lectures total this entire semester, and 3 of them were for the in-class assessment/tests that are proctored. It took 4 lectures to realize that this professor really isn't that good or fun to be around. Everything you need for this class is posted on canvas. Not a bad class, but a bad professor.

Rude and uncaring. Shared a concern with her and she told me to stop complaining and just do my work. Also followed syllabus for a late policy, and when she didn't count my project I told her I can submit for 10 percent late. She changed the syllabus to 10 points and gave me a zero on the project. No feedback nor any compassion or understanding Bad

she is worst possible professor I have ever seen. Too harsh and never cared about anything and judge pretty first. Its like being in the army camp in her class. And does not show any respect to any TA or students. Department should take strong steps and investigate against her.
Honestly not a very difficult class if you've taken ap csa, attendance not mandatory and just complete the labs on time and you'll be good

Margaret Ellis is very kind, and she cares about her students, but she doesn't know how to teach. During the lectures, she just answers people's questions from Piazza for 50 minutes. A lot of my projects (despite following all the guidelines perfectly) lost points for not commenting the way she wanted. The coursework itself is very easy.

Ellis was incredibly unprofessional and disrespectful as a professor. She did not seem to care for her students, and was very dismissive of issues. If possible, aim to take a different professor. This one will make your CS journey hell.

Very rude professor, lots of homework and labs that are a very tiny part of the grade, 0 feedback on some assignments that are graded harshly. Class feels like a high school class calling attendance and taking points off if you don't show up this is college not high school.

awful and not caring for any of her students. Doesn't even matter if WW3 happens, you need to go to lab or you lose all your points. Not compassionate with students problems and does not really help when you have the need. Does not communicate well requirements either or listen to questions. If you take her u might as well just look up YouTube vids

Cons: Neglects student concerns; disinterested in teaching; Dull, unhelpful lectures; most learning is self-directed via modules; Punishes students for VT system issues(via point deductions); Inefficient time-wasting policies for labs, assignments; Heavy tests; Lots of busy work Pros: Holds office hours; Available outside of class; Knows Java well.

She really cares about teaching and understands students' difficulties in learning Java and other CS topics (especially people who are new to coding). She is very approachable and truly cares about students' growth in the course topics. She answers our questions both in class and during office hours with passion.

Answers questions via a discussion portal so anyone can ask a question at any time of the day. She does her teaching through online modules and if you pay attention the exams are not bad at all and the labs use a lot of the same code as in the modules. Lectures aren't mandatory but if you are struggling on a project, she goes through useful info.

While the class was technically in-person, all the lectures were recordings from previous online classes. So really, it was just an async class. Every week, there's a decent amount of video lectures to watch with a section quiz at the end, but you can always speed up or rewatch the videos if you want. Projects aren't difficult, but start early!

I do not understand why the midterms and the final test are weighted more than the huge amount of other work that we need to do (labs, projects, quizzes, codworkouts, opendsa, etc.). She simply does not teach, I tried emailing her several times in which I did not even receive a response. The interactions I had with her made me confirm she was rude.

Doesnt actually lecture, just had video recordings from past years posted (which are mediocre at best). An insane amount of work for a 3 credit hour class. In response to complaints about my groupmates not participating in the project I was told to just do their code for them. Professor was rude and condescending in interactions I had with her.

Likes to do group projects. Probably to make it easier to grade. Doesn't take into consideration poor group members. States that if group members don't do the work you should do it for them to meet deadlines. Still gives the other members the same grade even though they don't do the work.

Rude, unnecessary hostile, lazy and boring. She doesnt even teach, you just watch her lectures from past years. I had a situation in which 5 of my 6 professors gave me extensions, and guess who didnt even care? I dont know a single person in my class who likes her and her class. Coding is fun, but surprisingly enough she can make it boring.

I felt that prof. Ellis really cared about her students the entire semester. She was always looking for ways to improve/get feedback. 2114 is just a hard class, no matter who you get, and I think you'd be lucky to have her as a prof. rather than anyone else.

She is somebody who understands programming and Java inside out. I feel like I will walk away from this class having a full understanding of data structures. The problem is that she isn't the best in terms of explaining things, but she's very knowledgeable and if you just put a little more effort in understanding her, you'll do fine.

After taking three years of CS classes in high school, I was greatly disappointed by Virginia Tech. While I have learned a lot in this class, the way Professor Ellis teaches is boring and uninspiring. There's way too much work and poorly written instruction to go through for each lab. This is not the way CS is meant to be taught.

The description for projects and labs are extremely awful, sometimes you can't even read what's her meaning of the steps. Can't even read what's the feedback of the project meaning. Huge amount of work with only a 3 credit class.
Rude teacher, extremely condescending.

The class as a whole is okay. I definately learned a lot from it, and Prof. Margaret Ellis gives a lot of lectures which are okay, however, she doesn't engage much with her class at all. She isn't at all a helpful professor to reach out too. Every question I've asked her wasn't helpful and you can tell she doesn't care about you or your concerns.

Understand some Java before taking this class. The whole class is assuming you know Java.  She's not a bad teacher, but she's a coder at heart, which makes her a more difficult teacher to deal with in terms of explaining. Still, Ellis is one of the best in the department. It's manageable.
Very nice and forgiving. All work is done is group projects. Easy grader.

The only bad thing I can say is that there was a lot of work for this class, but that is just the course itself, not the professor. She was so incredible, I loved being in her class. I would take her class again 1000x over. She is very accommodating and will work with you if you communicate and actually try in her class.

This class is so incredibly stupid. Half the stuff we do in class feels like kindergarten work. Sit near the back if you can so you can do other work. This problem comes from the way the department sets up the class though and is not entirely her fault. She is very nice and will help you but the class is a ginormous waste of time.

Marked attendance as mandatory because missing teamwork days without notifying the team and professor leads to a 10% penalty on the assignment that day. Nice professor. Make sure to complete all your work on time. Not super difficult, just that some of the grading is a bit strict, so utilize office hours + class time as needed before submitting

Twyman was good as an overall teacher but her grading system didnt make sense to me at all she is good in lectures but she is a tough grader the class overall is easy if you keep up with the assignments but I would advise you to choose an other prof instead of Twyman.

This was an extremely easy class, however Twyman as a teacher is terrible. Her policies make zero sense as to the weighting of certain negative incentives and certain requirements to avoid them. If you put in effort you will make it through this class with ease. I advise if you can avoid the hassle of having to deal with Twyman to do so.

Dr. Twyman is pretty relaxed. Attendance was checked but you could leave if the rest of class was individual or group work. Several classes were asynchronous throughout the semester. Class was very project heavy in terms of grades, but TA wasn't super harsh and they didn't take super long.
Dr.Twyman does a ton of talking in class and also is super particular with citations and will honor code you.

Prof Cat is amazing! I very much disliked the class, however, she is the perfect professor. As long as you get your work done, she lets you leave early if you want the majority of the time, but attendance is counted. The GTAs sucked for my class (harsh graders), but Twyman allows you to submit grade reviews if you disagree with a grade.

Workload is slight, content is easy, and she holds your hand through all of it. Just get a good group that's willing to work, do your own work and get assignments turned in, and you're guaranteed an A.

Enge 1215 is a completely useless class, but Prof Twyman made it more tolerable. I liked going to class and it seems like she really cares about the students. There was so much busywork in the class, which took lots of time, but it was a relatively easy A.

Can't blame twyman because this class just sucks and isn't fun. Almost all busy work and none of it besides matlab and makerspace felt like learning engineering that was useful to me. (and even those were dragged out into different boring writing) This class is just annoying and you have to get through it
Catherine Twyman is a great professor. She is very helpful, nice, and cares about her students. If you just do all the work, you will get an A in 1225.

Definitely Prof. Twyman is lecture heavy, so it does get boring, but I will say she makes this class easy to run through the semester. She's nice and lenient so have a word with her about your absences or late work if you have a reason.

The only time attendance was mandatory was when a group project was due within a week. But if you couldn't make it you could email her and she would understand. She made learning MATLAB really easy so I would recommend her if you are new to coding. The lectures are boring but all ENGE 1215 classes get the same homework and she grades nicely.

Twyman herself was pretty chill - fast email responses, grants extension requests before the due date, easy to get an A as long as you do the work. Half of the assignments were group work so as long as your group gets their work done you should be fine. If not, she's pretty good about making sure everyone is doing their part.

Prof. Twyman is great! She's amazing with extensions(if you ask she will give you one)and is really good at responding to emails on time.If you have a good group this class is a breeze but if you don't like what I did she likes to step in and whip the group into shape if that doesn't work she will always recognize the work you individually put in.

I took this class in Fall 2022, and the class was easy because of my group. There were solely engineering students in the Fall, so the majority of the class had that good work ethic. Twyman tries to engage the class and seems like she cares about what the is teaching. Extremely understanding when projects don't go as expected. Just talk to her.

The class was pretty easy, but it depends on the group you get assigned. If everyone in your group does their work, the class will be a breeze. She reads straight from the board which is kind of boring, but overall a fine class.
The class is incredibly boring and she tends to drag out lectures but other than that she's fine. She cares about her students and is receptive to their needs but the class sucks.

More writing than my ENGL1105 class. Not difficult, but a lot. As long as your groupmates do not all skip class and do no work, it should be very manageable to get an A if you follow the rubrics. As a professor, she was good but not anything special.

Although ENGE 1215 can be great or awful depending on your assigned group, Professor Twyman was very supportive the entire semester. She is very easy to approach and gives good feedback on your work. You will have to put in work and attend class, but it's an easy A with at least a half decent group.

Prof. Twyman was just an okay professor. Attendance was mandatory, but there wasn't much content taught in class. Often you would show up just for her to say that it was a work day. Pretty much the only useful part of the class was the MATLAB unit. As far as personality, she was polite and understanding of any issues you may have.

Professor Twyman's class is definitely more difficult than the other professors which was my only issue with the class. We got more assignments and lower grades on projects than other 1215 students, however, the class is fine. If you stay on top of the work you'll get an A. I would take the class again no problem, and I learned a lot of matlab

She did her job but thats about it. There's a fun segment at the beginning then just power point slides guiding the class that she puts out before hand. Attendance was not mandatory and I recommend not going because the walk is far and the curriculum is useless just help your group and youll be fine.

Very chill class with Professor Twyman, the course is essentially just group projects and papers will a little bit of matlab sprinkled in, and in the latter half of the course most of the class time is you and your team's own time to work on your project, so the homework in this class is very manageable.
Professor Twyman was one of the best professors I've ever had! She is very caring towards her students, and as long as you put in the effort you will do well!

Professor Twyman really cares about the success of each student in her classes. The group I was assigned for the class didn't do their fair share of work, however, after some emailing, she became aware of the issue and accommodated me for the problem. She is very willing to help students.
I would recommend professor Twyman. She is really forgiving and gave me a couple extensions. It is a lot of group work, and the lecture can be boring but its an easy A if you do the work.

Prof. Twyman was a very nice person, just not a great teacher. There are many group projects, and too many papers as well. It seemed more like busywork than actually learning engineering. Going to class wasn't very helpful most of the time. Just pray for a good team and look at the rubric when doing assignments.

She is a very nice lady who does assign a good bit of work. I do not know why people are complaining because the work she assigns does not take that long, it is more busy work to understand fundamentals.

Easily the worst professor I had. She lacks confidence in her own ability to teach, and never gives a proper answer to the questions that are asked to her. She brings up her personal life at the beginning of class too much (nobody cares, move on), and she gives us paper, after paper. It's more of an English class at this point.

Twyman was an OK professor, but I had her for her first semester teaching. For most assignments, she was unclear on what she wanted so I had to ask for clarification on most things. Her advice was not always helpful to the assignment itself, but her TAs explained things well. She was however a very nice lady and would try her best to aid students

Dr. Dubik is a wonderful! Super caring and really strives to make sure students feel welcome in the class and doesn't make you feel stupid for asking question lol. He's incredibly personable and down to earth, really good vibes all around !! He's able to break down concepts really well and made this class one of the ones I understand the most.
Really good at explaining difficult topics. Also incredibly responsive to students' comments/questions.
so strict and feel bad

She teaches a communications class, but can't communicate what she expects out of each assignment. Will take off points for random things not on the rubric. She doesn't feel human at all, almost robotic.

Very patronizing professor. She doesn't seem to care about her female students, especially when they are being excluded in male-dominated spaces. More focused on being addressed formally than engaging with student concerns in a meaningful way.
For a simple class about grammar and putting together a report, the grading is super harsh. Dr. Carper runs the class very strictly even though the TAs do all of the work.

I don't know why Carper has such good reviews. She is a really hard grader and literally will not help you with anything because she makes her TA's do everything. I think she is the only option for 3034 which sucks

Dr. Carper was an amazing professor! Her lectures were very informative. She gave good feedback throughout the semester. Make sure you pull you weight in your group, as your participation is a big part of your grade!

I really enjoyed Dr. Carper's class, she's a great professor.  This class is all about learning to write standard and professional reports and presentations. Your teammates rating of you account for a large percentage of your grade, so make sure to pull your own weight.

This class was a roller coaster. My group had to claw are way back up to a C to an A. We bombed our first big assignment. This seems to happen a lot in the class, and it definitely teaches you to be perseverant. The class can feel really extra / picky at times, but Carper is super willing to help outside class.

I love him! As someone with no coding experience, he truly makes this class bearable. Lectures are live coding so def go. He explains things very clearly and simply and also makes it entertaining. Can't recommend enough! Easy workload and very straightforward.

I loved taking this class! Professor Lewis was a really nice person and instructor, and while some of the assignments may have been a bit difficult (like the individual projects), if you take the time to do them properly and seek help when you don't understand something, then you will do good in this class.

Lewis is probably the best and only professor that teaches CS 1064. He's funny and answer any questions you have and likes to strike up a conversation with students. Just do the assignments and read the class text and you would be fine.

Dr Lewis was a good professor and explains everything very well. I have no interest in coding (I had to take this class) so the lecture were very boring. It is overall an easy class and you should take Dr Lewis if you can.

Dr. Lewis was very chill, but gave a lot of assignments. That being said, they were all fairly easy besides the programming projects. He assigns them weeks before they are due, so start on them in advance. His lectures were very straightforward, lecturing in Thonny (the programming software) as compared to traditional slides.

I have never coded before and got an A. The way the class is structured is completely idiotic, focusing on Ticketmaster programs and useless Madlibs generators for projects instead of data analytics (what python is good at). John Lewis is a very good lecturer and is a very strong speaker. His demonstrations are very clear and the readings are easy.
One of the best professors I've ever had. He breaks things down into normal people terms and stops very frequently for questions. As long as you actually do the readings you'll do good in this class.

I would take this class at a community college if possible (unless you are a CS major). As someone with zero coding background, I felt like Lewis expected too much of his students. TAs grade the quizzes (4 in sem.), essays (2 in sem.), and projects (3 in sem.). Their grading can be all over the place (lax or harsh). Lecture is just live coding.

Although his lectures are consisted of live coding examples that could be entirely learnt from the online textbook, he's generous for providing relatively easy extra credit for the class along with being helpful during office hours! Quizzes aren't too bad and go to the TAs for the programming projects.

If you don't have any background in Python you likely will struggle, however, this doesn't mean he's a bad prof. You can tell he wants to help you learn, and uses lots of real world examples and makes it fun as to keep students engaged.

he's so great and so patient. this class was easy for me bc i have coded before in a different language, but this class is super accessible even if you're a complete beginner. do the readings at the beginning of each week and you'll be completely fine
Least favorite class taken in college.

Dr. Lewis is AWESOME! I've taken CS classes before, but his course truly made me feel like I was finally confident in my programming skills. His lectures are live coding demonstrations, so it helps to do the reading/hw beforehand. He is a super knowledgable professor and genuinely cares about his students.
I love john lewis, best atVT
He was an incredible professor. Really loved taking his class and the material to the point that I decided to minor in CS.

His lectures are just live coding examples, and classes will generally be empty after a week or two, although he tries to make them fun. Very introductory material, so if you already know how to program in another language, you'll be fine as long as you do the reading.  Projects have very clear rubrics. Do the extra credit, it's worth a ~1.2% bump.

prof lewis went through lectures and explained things as if we have never coded in our lives before. the textbook readings aligned with what was went over in class which helped a lot, and by finding extra credit 'easter eggs' in the readings it helped my grade a lot !! this man was great

Funny guy, and he's respectful towards students. If you're not a fan of sitting and looking at code, lectures can get a little boring, but I feel like that's the nature of CS lectures. You can get extra credit for finding easter eggs in the textbook. It's just italicized text, and they can be pretty funny.

My actual class time was at 1:25 but he let me sit in his earlier class. LOVE THIS GUY he's also funny which makes his lectures a little more interesting. Theres not really many allowance for late work but THERES EXTRA CREDIT at the end and its pretty easy to get an A if u do well on the projects and ok on the exams

Class is made up of weekly homework assignments based on reading (first try), weekly coding exercises, 2 simple essays, 4 quizzes, and 3 projects. If you put in the work by coming to class and utilizing the TAs, you will be fine! Love Dr. Lewis he is a king
Time restrictions on quizzes were a little too short for comfort. But overall chill class. I liked the easter eggs hidden in the website used to teach the class.

He is funny and his lectures are generally pretty good but definitely got boring. The homework every week was manageable and the projects were the thing I spent most of my time on. It is a good amount of work but you should be able to do pretty well if you study and give yourself time for the projects.
Lectures are very helpful although not required. If you go to the lectures, 1064 is an easy class. Dr. Lewis is passionate and is very down to earth and modest. I would highly recommend.

Prof Lewis is a great teacher! Even though the lectures are literally just the textbook, he makes sure to also write examples of the code and explain confusing processes in detail. Make sure to redo the exercises and practice in Thonny for the quizzes. The projects may get confusing, but he details everything he needs in the rubric. TAs help a lot!

Amazing professor! He'll throw small jokes throughout the lecture to keep the class engaged which was fun. The class itself was pretty easy, you work solely through the online textbook that he tells you to buy and there was 4 short quizzes/midterms you have to do. There are also 3 projects throughout the semester but I recommend utilizing the TA's.

Dr. Lewis is a funny professor and the class itself isn't very difficult. If you read the textbook (which is required for assignments), and understand, you don't really need to show up to class. There are also lots of office hours for TA's and you're guaranteed to find someone to help you.

Class is mostly copying code but its all posted on Canvas. Projects aren't too bad if you start early, and his office hours/the TA's are very helpful. Put in effort for quick checks, they're worth more than you expect (he gives extra credit with them!). I didn't know about python coming in, and i really enjoyed the class.

Extremely beginner-friendly, I came in with 0 knowledge of Python and excelled in the class. Make sure to start on projects early. There is no reason to show up to class if you're able to just read off Rephactor and understand what it's asking you to do. In-class lectures tend to just be reciting off Rephactor pages.
No background in python is necessary. Class is very straightforward. The projects can be a little tricky but there are a ton of TAs to help.

Dr. Lewis is a very nice professor and exceptional at teaching. There is a lot of work for the class, especially for a 1XXX level, but it ensures that you understand what you're doing. Office hours both with Dr. Lewis and the TAs are beneficial, and you get a lot out of the class. Definitely take if you're even considering
He was a good professor and understanding with grades. Notes are important to go over. You get the grade of the work you put into the class. He also provides extra credit and easy 100% grades.

This class made me develop a passion for programming.  Definitely get some background knowledge of Python before you start the class.  The structure of the course was one of the best throughout my college career, and Prof. Lewis is an amazing instructor.  The only problem I had was the strict grading by the TA's on the projects.

During class time Lewis normally just writes code that you copy down. It is hard to learn with little to no notes to look back on. You have to go to office hours as a new python user to consider passing.
Hard to learn, most of the time you just copy what he writes in class.
John Lewis at the start seems to be a caring person, but as a professor he does not meet expectations. The projects were way to hard for just starting to learn python.

Lewis continues to make his course harder year by year for no reason. The projects in his class should not be considered for beginners. Very little mention for what will be on quizzes until 1-2 days prior of the quiz.

Very nice and funny guy. I never went to lectures but went to office hours often. Please don't be dumb and Chegg the projects like a good portion of my classmates did this semester. If you go to TA office hours, they are glad to help you out. I had little/no programming background and did well.

Your average professor that can be respected. He is very loud, so don't worry about not being able to hear him from the far back of the room. Class is very doable, so long you have good time management. Very clear grading criteria that does not turn you a mess like CS1114 does.

Took him in Spring 2022. A very nice teacher in-person. He speaks loud and clear, so don't worry about not being able to hear him in the back. Do your assignments and projects EARLY, so if you have any questions, you can attend office hours. Be careful while doing textbook assignments, as you can get penalized if you just mindlessly choose.
If you do the bare minimum, you should be able to pass this class with a B+/A- minimum. He is a nice guy and passionate about what he teaches.  Not a lot of work, just stay on track of things.
If u understand python dont go to the lectures. Easy to understand to code, it took me a month but u have to do the assignment when its posted.

Easy class especially if you have programming experience. Only show up for the first day or if you are about to go over something you want to understand. All the homework is easy, projects aren't hard if you start them early. He rounded my grade from B to A- because I emailed him AND put in the work. If you try to learn, you will pass.

When I went to Professor Lewis's class, he went over the material in a very simple and easily understandable way. He taught Python concepts in a hands-on way by coding as a class. However, if you have a somewhat decent understanding of the basics of programming, you do not need to attend the lectures very often.

Very fun class! He does expect some effort from students to participate in class, so read and pay attention! The projects were super fun and easy to get 100s on. Homework was easy as long as you read the online textbook. Nice guy and very helpful when I had questions about the projects, etc.

TBH u don't need to come to class, u need to buy his rephracter online hw thing to do the class. All the reading HW is on quizlet expect for the weekly exercise in which u need to do the reading to figure out how to write it or go to Office hours. Every so often he will assign a project and u have to go to office hours to get done, they'll do for u

Class is fine, professor is good. Pretty easy. You can get away with not showing up to a single class if you have some programming experience. The final is only 10% of our grade but is 120 questions which I find kind of ridiculous.

I enjoyed this class. Professor Lewis is very cool. I had no issues, but I had some previous python experience from a high school class. The class is focused on 5 coding projects. As long as you start them early and come to class, you shouldn't have any issues. He often demonstrates aspects of the projects in class. Attend office hours if you need.

Dr. Lewis is very knowledgeable and sprinkles in humor with his presentations. The class focuses heavily on 5 semester coding projects which are quite easy for the most part. There are multiple TAs that essentially give you office hours for most hours on weekdays, and they can be a great help whenever you run into probems on your projects.

He is well informed and gives clear lectures while answering questions. Attendance really helps with understanding the material. His grading system is well balanced between reading checks, projects, a midterm, and a final. It requires some work, attention, and trial and error to do well, but it is a great intro class for a programming language!

Intro to Python at VT is one of the most neglected courses at the school. For a class that should be used to engage people in CS, prof John Lewis is a boring presenter and a tough grader. If you don't code EXACTLY the way he wants you to, you are doing it wrong. Take it from a CS major who has 3 years experience with python, learn it on udemy.
He is a good lecturer, I never needed to see him after class but I know he was available. Does not matter if you miss class, the notes will be posted for you. Overall good guy.

This class will be easy if you have any programming knowledge, otherwise it can be challenging. But there are so many TAs, so if you take advantage of the office hours it's do-able. He's a fun guy and creates a positive vibe in the lecture hall. He's good at explaining stuff.

If you have some knowledge of how to code, then you'll excel in this class. The lectures would just go over writing some specific code, and since it was a 500+ person lecture, I didn't have to show up all the time. There are some textbook homework problems, but they are pretty easy. Some of the tas' of this class were also helpful.

Great CS professor.. he makes sure you understand the material. He was an amazing professor for a 500 person class. There wasnt a lot of homework, but coding projects are something you need to start early.

Spectacular lectures, really cares about us doing well not just in the class, but in the future. Relates things to the real world. Showed us instagram reels one time, amazing.

If you haven't taken a physics/circuits related class before, you need to go above and beyond to put effort into this class. Ball was a pretty good professor. Dr.Ball is an excellent teacher who makes a genuine effort to remember students by name. He's approachable and is always willing to help. The class itself isn't too difficult, but his tests carry 15% more weight than Professor Dunning.

While 1004 can be a tough course, he explained most topics quite well, and whatever I didn't understand I could easily look up as there are so many great resources. Overall, the tests weren't too hard, and while some lectures can be boring they are usually pretty interesting.

Ball really knows his stuff and is an amazing lecturer. The lectures sometimes dragged, but he teaches the material so well and applies it to the real world. Genuinely get him for any class you can, because it all feels useful and meaningful with him.
Great professor. Get him for any class you can.

Dr. Ball is one of the best professors in the ECE department, hands down. I've had him for both 1004 and 2024, and both times I've come out with an appreciation of how well he lectures. Such a great prof. I want to take as many classes with Dr. ball as I can. He knows almost every student by name and has great stories and anecdotes to relate to class. Overall great.

He's a chill guy. Lectures were fun even if they were hard to understand. He's also really good at making everything practical which helps a lot with understanding. Easily one of the best professors I've ever had.

Amazing professor for ECE 1004. Relates the concepts in class to his time in industry a lot and that really helped put things in perspective and think about practicality. Dr. Ball is a great teacher, gave good lectures, and always responded fast to emails. I definitely would have failed if I hadn't had him as my professor for this class. His office hours were very helpful and you can definitely tell that he cares a lot about his students.

I think a lot of the lower ratings had a really hard time understanding the topics in ECE. He know his stuff but it was a really hard class to begin with and complicated topics. Great professor and great lecturer. Very smart, sometimes expects more than students can handle. Relates material to real life, knows everything there is to know about circuits. Friendly and helpful. Professor McPherson always brings so much energy to the class and presents everything very clearly. Best teacher at tech, it's an easy A if you pay attention cause he teaches the matieral so well you're almost guaranteed to understand it.

Honestly overrated imo. Though cheerful and energetic, I could barely pay attention in her lectures. Projects were also a massive and unexpected spike in difficulty in comparison to assignments beforehand. Does not really engage with students outside of class other than one hour of OH per week.
Great professor. As you'll see by other reviews the projects can take a bit of time though.

Great professor. Embedded is mostly graded off of the quizzes, homework, and projects. As long as you stay on top of those, you'll be fine. That said, its really easy to get lost if you don't keep up with the material along the way. Overall, Dr. Ali has been one of the best professors I've taken in ECE so far though.

Dr. Ali is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is engaging, explains topics clearly, and cares a lot about the students. The class was not too difficult, but I learned a lot about embedded systems. 10/10 would take again.

Easily my favorite CPE professor. Very good lectures, cares a lot about her students, and you can just tell she really enjoys teaching. You are allowed to implement extra stuff for your projects for extra credits, and she is REALLY generous with those (usually you get 20% maximum for each project). I was an EE major and I added CPE after this class
Absolutely incredible lecturer. Very kind and open outside of class. Definitely cares about her teaching style and is willing to change based on feedback. Take her courses every chance you get.

Dr. Nazhand-Ali is one of the best professors you can get for ECE, but it does not mean the course concepts are easy. She has lots of ways to keep you on track during lectures and gives fantastic analogies of how things work. Make sure you start projects as early as possible and go to office hours, you will be ok.

She is a great teacher. Very helpful. Go to office hours, she will explain topics that are unclear. She will regrade your test if you need it. Overall, one of the best teachers I had in the ECE department. Homeworks are easy and tests and projects are average.
Unrealistic grading standarts and not enough help.
Homeworks were easy, lots of group work that counts for a lot of the grade, but criteria is clear. Tests are somewhat difficult too

I've never cared to write a professor review, but she was amazing. Go to class and pay attention—the homework is doable. If you're stuck, she posts videos that will help a lot. In-class work is extra credit. She's super helpful and even helped me explore Land Dev and connect me with a company that led to an internship. Best professor I've ever had

Claire is SO nice. Her class was pretty easy especially if you just pay attention to lectures. She is good at answering questions and she cares about her students a lot. Wants to get to know everyone and always made me feel welcomed and happy. I hope ti take a class with her again.

Claire's sustainable land development class has a good mix of hands-on activities, guest speakers, field trips, and readings. All of the work felt like it was valuable while I was doing it and I felt like I learned a lot in this course.
Claire White is the best teacher ive had at tech

All the work is on the computer and you must print out assignments during the first couple of months. Pretty easy class since she gives pdfs on what to do and which tools to incorporate. Offers extra credit through participation in class, a very loose grader, and work is easy to follow.

Super boring class, and her personality does nothing to make up for it. Doesn't actually teach any of the information on the exams, so you basically have to teach yourself if you want to get a good grade in the class. Would definitely avoid if you have any options for her class.

Intelligent professor whose class is more interactive and hands-on than traditional textbook approach - the problem? Vague information, lack of reading, and no concrete material to study with. Exams are difficult because of this and homework is unrealistically graded to high expectations.

CAD is a fun class, and isn't meant to be stressful by any means. Homeworks were lengthy but they were posted minimum 2-3 weeks before the deadline. No tests (just weekly quizzes), and no final. Also the last 3 classes she gave extra credit if you showed up and participated.
Just Llike Mrs.White but better

Dr.Young is the best professor I have had at Virginia Tech. Though I found his tests pretty difficult, I liked his lectures and personality. He's very caring and encouraging. I worked super hard and he did not ignore that but really appreciated it.

Easy lectures but long tests that are mostly memorization. Labs count for a lot of this class so that's the most important part really. Overall minimal effort class with not much homework but labs certainly make up for that.
Wonderful professor, takes the time to try and learn everyone's name.

Kevin's CAD class was a lot of fun and he made it very enjoyable to go to. Be warned that the last half of the semester covers Revit, which is taught by "Tom Powers", not Kevin, who is terrible and made the end of the semester miserable in this class. Be prepared to spend 10+ hours on a single Revit assignment so don't put it off.

Kevin is an amazing professor in the CEE department. He has plenty of real-world experience that he incorporates into his lectures, and takes the time to thoroughly explain content. Very manageable and enjoyable class, easy A with some effort. TAKE IT IN THE FALL! The lab is outdoors and you'll be miserable in the spring semester's winter.

I love his teaching style. First goes over concepts, and then uses them to go over numerical problems. Very clear about what we should expect on exams. Also is ok with students calling him Kevin. Super chill dude.

Fantastic professor with a very fair workload. Teaches clearly and concisely. If you follow along with the lectures, the assignments should be a breeze. There is little opportunity to access information outside of class time so make use of it.
Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had at Tech. His lectures are very straight forward, and he is aways willing to help when it's needed. 11/10 would take again.
He makes lectures fun but really heavy grading and work also hard  to communicate(he doesnt answer emails.)
Hard class but an amazing teacher. Gets points across and teaches accurately and very well. Incredible professor.

Scardina is a true professor. He is very enthusiastic about the topics and wants you to learn. You HAVE to learn to pass this class. You NEED to start strong its hard to come back as its ALL cumulative. Its hard for a reason. PAY attention, take notes, actively do hw, seek help and be invested in understanding and learning the class. Great teacher.
Awfu! Very hard class because the test has nothing to do with his lectures. He seems to enjoy failing 50% of the class.

Probably my first "real" professor at Virginia Tech. He is a true professional which I cannot say about many professors now-a-days. I wish all my engineering classes were taught by people like him as we would actually have competent engineers in the world.

Scardina's classes are tough - I choose to take another one of his classes because I thought he was an excellent teacher though. He's the best proffessors I've had. He teaches extremely well. You'll have to work hard but it's worth it. In other classes you don't understand or retain things that well, but in his class you will.

Scardina makes the class so much harder than it has to be. Content wise its not the worse class, but he is horrible on grading and will take off points for random things. Also better not show up late to the lab because thats an instant 2 zeros on lab reports. You will leave the class understanding everything but still have nothing to show for it

This class is extremely hard compared to Statics and Deforms here at Virginia Tech. Scardina is a very tough grader and is more than willing to fail you if he sees fit; this past semester, Spring 2021, over 60 people took "W's" across his sections with an average GPA of 2.14 across both his Fluids sections.

Lectures are fairly smooth, but the tests are EXTREMELY hard compared to the homework assigned throughout the semester. He grades the test very hard, and harps on the idea that he only "presents" the material and that we should teach it to ourselves. I got B+ in both statics and deforms, but this class you really have to work for.

Took him freshman year (senior now), and he is still the worst professor I've had. His grading system was ridiculous - your entire grade was basically determined by your final exam. He used to talk about students emails too... Not sure if that's even allowed.

I struggled a bit in this class because I had absolutely no prior coding experience, but I ended up with a really high grade because of how things are weighted at the end of the semester. You have 6 free passes where you can reattempt any assignment or retake a quiz which absolutely saved my grade many times. Go to his office hours if you need help
Not a good professor would not take it again. Lectures are not clear. The class is carried by TA's and even that is not enough.

Going into this class I had zero java experience and basic python knowledge, in my opinion your success is really determined by the amount of work you put in and if the interactive readings work for your learning style (which they did for me). The programs are a lot of work, the labs are usually okay, and lectures are skippable.

Not good at all, just avoid taking him. He makes way too many changes near the end of the semester and messes with your grade. The class has good support though from TAs and Piazza. Just a horrible professor.
the worst tbh.

This course is designed for beginners who are ambitious to study cs in the future. What's more annoying is the EMRN and the finals is so difficult. Programs are hard and take a long time for beginners, and is frankly frustrating. Lectures are so boring and code workout doesn't work anytime. NOT A BEGINNER COURSE. TAKE CREDIT IF POSSIBLE OR CC.

Chill guy, he is a great proffessor, lectures are good but you gotta study a lot by yourself. The programs are hard and most of what you will be studying is practiced thru them. TAs genuinely suck. This class does have a steep learning curve. The concept of free passes is very thoughtful. Prof edwards OH are very good.

Easily the worst teacher ive ever had. Class is physically impossible TA's dont even know how to do his assignments. His lectures are useless. The programs are impossible to do, his grading system for code(which he invented) is so pointless and annoying. Never heard a good thing about him or the class. If it wasn't obvious do not take him.

Terrible teacher. Assigns weekly reading and labs every week of the semester. On top of that assigns difficult programs that ask you to basically cure cancer and includes topics never done in class. Then doesn't even talk about them in class and lectures about some basic concepts covered in the reading. This is not an intro class.

The entire curriculum was redone for the 2024-2025 school year, making this course less work and easier. He gave six free passes, so there was no stress if you didn't complete a program in time. You can basically only fail this course now if you don't put in the effort. Make sure to start your programming assignments early, and you will be fine.

Professor Stephen Edwards was an okay professor. The lectures don't teach you much and you should be ready to self-teach yourself. At the time I took the course, he used an ERMC grading scale which makes passing more difficult. Some of the projects you are required to complete need out of box thinking which many new coders struggle with greatly.
Lectures are extremely boring. He rambles on. Will not help you make up if you get sick. Tests are ridiculously hard. Will never study under him again.

Very passionate with Computer Science and genuinely enjoys teaching the course. Be prepared for a very heavy workload because dear goodness, this course consumes more hours out of all the classes I have for this semester. Coursework is shared with Professor Barnette, so be prepared for possible delays and bugs in assignments.

CS 1114 is a terribly designed course, which was designed by Dr. Edwards. The lectures were pretty useless unless there was a quiz that you had to take that day. The program grading scale of EMRN was extremely harsh. Office hours were always way too crowded because nothing is covered in the lectures.

This class was definitely not for the faint-hearted and did a good job teaching me CS for the first time. However, you have to be very willing to think outside of the box and work hard on the later programs. Late penalty very generous, I got a 50 on things and still came out with an A so its very doable. This will be your most time consuming class.

One of the worst intro to coding courses you could take, a weed out class. Without prior coding experience, it will be very hard to succeed. Half of the people I knew in the class either dropped it or failed the course. The EMRC grading scale was incredibly harsh and coursework took up more time than the rest of my classes combined. DON'T RECOMMEND

The most stressful class I have ever taking in my life. I remember consoling my classmates after they were crying about how difficult and stressful this class is. He uses the EMRC grading scale which is ridiculously harsh. More than half of the class dropped the class. The majority of those who stayed ended up failing the class after the final.
Had a A for the entire semester, had a panic attack during the final and since it was the entirety of my grade finished with a D+. Go hokies!

I was told this class was going to be hard work. Starting with no coding experience was hard, but this class taught me, if not by trial by fire. Stephen not only clearly hates teaching but also hates the people he teaches, as shown by his horrendous grading. His experimental scale left me with 2 options, pass all 40 assignments, or fail and die.

The class was easy the first couple weeks but by program 6: hell. If you've had previous experience coding you'll probably get through, but as a beginner this class seriously made me rethink all of my life choices. Be ready to do the work and don't delay doing the assignments. Everyone I knew withdrew, and the grading system is horrible.

This class had a lot of work each week and was hard to keep up with. It has no pre-requisites but without prior coding knowledge, it will be very hard to pass and succeed. It takes up a lot of time and requires you to apply knowledge to complete assignments that you haven't learned. Also, the assignment directions for the programs are vague.

Yea its really a hit or miss with many of the CS professors here at VT. I would say he isn't the worst but he also isn't the best. TAs are helpful but hard to get them. Do your work on time. The freaking reading assignments are god awfully glitchy so beware.

He seems to like CS and CS itself which is good. Only thing is the class is incredibly hard to get through. For a beginner course as someone who has never coded this class is making me reconsider a CS degree. If you plan to take the class, learn some java because it feels awful at the moment

Stephen is literally my favorite person. He seems to genuinely enjoy teaching CS, and consistently encourages those with little to no experience--which makes sense because it's an intro class, but that unfortunately isn't always a given. Plus, his Hawaiian shirts are sick (hold bets with your friends before class over which color it'll be that day)

This was a required class for computer science. This class seriously made me rethink my major. I hated every second of it. Labs and projects were vague and hard to understand. Tests were crazy hard. My TA was decent, but the Edwards is extremely unhelpful. Never actually answers questions and never likes to admit when he is wrong or unfair.

This professor seems alright during class and in lectures but the work gets tough pretty much after the first exam. This class starts easy then gets exponentially harder every week. Be prepared to work hard. The Lab assignments that he posts online are not as descriptive and do not help when doing the Labs or projects. Best of Luck.

Dr. Sevak is an insanely knowledgeable professor. He is very direct and straightforward. He provides a lot of homework, I'd say redo them many times. He makes the final exams that were harder than expected. However, pay attention, go to office hours, ask questions, do the homework, and understand why, or you are going to suffer the consequences.

Took him for both dynamics and mechanical vibrations. I can tell you that his classes are challenging, BUT NOT IMPOSSIBLE. I can confidently say that I have learned a lot and retained the info very well. I think he is a good professor if you're willing to try and put in the effort. I never thought I couldn't pass his classes. Go to office hours!!!!

Enjoyed this class.  Sevak is smart, his lectures are very boring though, didn't go to many of them.  Homeworks were a little intense, but I found his tests to be INCREDIBLY straight forward and thus easy, making my life in this class easier compared to others.  Would recommend his section for an easy A.

Lectures are not very engaging, but Tahmasian is knowledgeable and clearly enjoys dynamics. Homeworks are a bit time-consuming, and the lectures alone were not always enough for me. Even though it's not mandatory, get Bolton's textbook and supplement with that!!!!

Lectures are monotone and nap inducing. He does 2 - 3 example problems over a 75 minute class period, while going at a snail's pace. He assigns multiple large homework assignments every week, including midterm weeks. He does not teach all the material before assigning homework problems and do not count on the online textbook for any help.
Tests are pretty hard, but pretty similar to homework and practice tests. Definitely one of the hardest classes I've ever taken.

Sevak is an amazing teacher, but gives really difficult tests. His lectures are very helpful and he is really good at explaining the content. He gives quite a bit of homework, and his tests are pretty hard. He usually won't curve, and if he does it's so the average reaches around a C. If you really put in the work then it shouldn't be that bad.

Most of the other reviews are still valid. He really does care about his students doing well and will help you in office hours, although he won't just give you the answer. My only gripe is that his voice can get soft at times, so just down a coffee beforehand and you'll be fine. Aside from that, he's a fantastic prof and I'd definitely recommend!

Sevak is a very good teacher. He is fairly soft-spoken but you can tell he enjoys teaching and cares a lot about the class. Test questions were always easier than homework questions. Tests are 5 questions on paper with a 2 hour limit. For homework, Sevak uses WILEY plus, which gives no partial credit, and the questions are needlessly complex.

He gets a bad rap for no reason. Genuinely so sweet. His lectures are a bit boring but super informative - you don't need to study any material outside of his lectures if you pay attention enough. Super helpful office hours, lots of homework but tests are very comparable to the hw so it's worth putting in the effort. LOVE HIM

Dynamics is a very hard class. In class, he just uses the projector to write down notes and do example problems. His homework problems are also time consuming because he uses pictures from the textbook and changes the pictures by using softwares and therefore creating his own questions. Midterms are slightly easier than the homeworks. Good luck!
Its a hard class you have to put your time into it. GTA office hours better than his. Would take another teacher

I had an excellent experience with Prof. Tahmasian. Most of the exam questions were recycled homework / classwork questions, so if you practice, you'll do well. This class's homework is time-consuming, but if you do not cheat and actually practice, you will do well. A lot of engineers coasted through high school, but it simply does not work here.

I thought his lectures were very informative, but very boring. It's hard to stay focussed the whole time, but extremely benificial if you do. He gives lots of examples in class and gives good partial credit on tests. This course requiers a lot of time for studying & doing homework, so be ready for that. Tests get increasingly more difficult.

Overall difficult class but Sevak teaches it pretty well. The units are clear cut and he provides example problems in class. The homeworks are usually very challenging and will take up a lot of your time. The tests are difficult as well but he gives a lot of partial credit as long as you put in some effort on the problem.

Caring professor who wants his students to pass. Solves problems in class and posts notes after every lecture. Assigns a lot of HW which are harder than exams. Sometimes extends Homework which is nice. Go to office hours he's very helpful! 4 midterms and a final, and he sometimes curves. Drops 2 HWs at the end and his grading scale is different.

Sevak is a chill and friendly guy. He does problems in class that are similar to tests. There are two 8-9 online homework problems on Wiley plus per week. Tests can be confusing, which is normal for any statics class. He curves tests to around 73. He grades pretty fast if he is not busy.

Sevak's teaching style is come to class, do the notes, and spend quite the time on homework. Even though he always says people call him boring who cares!! He prepares us well for the tests, answers questions well in class, helps a lot in office hours and is really nice. Have fun spending hours on wiley plus ;P.

Not the most entertaining, but Sevak is a good guy and a good teacher. He really knows what he's talking about and hes work is precise and easy to follow. He does proofs and practice problems in class and often gives you some of the homework answers for free. He gives fair partial credit for tests and is fast at grading.

Do not expect to understand any of the material. Dynamics is a hard class to teach, all Sevak did was derive formulas and rush through problems on blanks sheets of paper. No format to the lectures, and roundabout ways of answering questions. Test were way harder than homework's and in-class problems and almost always curveball questions.
Statics is a hard class in general, if you're not physics based... good luck. I cry at night, it is quite haunting.

If you take him for dynamics be prepared to learn from the textbook and youtube. He just derives formulas in class expects you to memories them then speeds through a problem so ur stuck just copying to keep up. Impossible to learn.

I'm giving Tasmanian the benefit of the doubt because dynamics is very tough course to teach; however, his class did not cut it for me. He teaches by projecting problems and walking through them, but I found this to not be helpful. He assigns a lot of HW, and I found his exams to be a lot harder than the HW and worked through class problems.

When I took this class it was an absolute mess, I got through statics and even deforms with a lot less trouble than Dr. Tahmasian's dynamics class. Our test grades were so bad that the grading had to be changed mid semester.

Professor Tahmasian is really great. If you dont understand the material, go to his office hours and he will work with you until you get it. Homework is difficult but the tests are always easier than homework so they prepare you well. And he always posts the class notes on canvas

His Majesty, the King. He cares about his students A LOT and wants us to learn well. He "will push homework back" and make the last week super busy (so we should work ahead). Statics is a breeze; deform is a gale. 26+1 HWs, 15%. Missing a HW isn't a big deal, but doing and reviewing HW helps a lot learn the material. Aced the midterms and final.

You will work in this class. A lot. His accent can also be a bit difficult to get used to and he has FOUR midterms. If anything describes the class in a nutshell, that's it. Thing is, he's actually very caring about his students; he will look at how busy you are during the week and will push homework back if other classes are busy during that week.

He teaches from a document camera: "Professor, the camera's too bright and we can't see what you're writing down, can you please change the brightness?" "No." Most of your learning should come from intuition and knowledge from previous classes, not from actually learning stuff in this class.

Sevak is a very good professor in my opinion. At first he may seem a little reserved, and his accent may turn some people off. After having him for a semester I really like him because of his office hours. He will spend the time with you until you figure out a problem. His accent is nothing to be concerned about, and he's a genuinely nice person.

Awful professor. Disorganized lectures and weekly quizzes with little time. Answers questions with little detail and gets sidetracked easily. Way too much homework compared to other professors. Almost never available for office hours, and answers nothing when he does have them. Provided less help material compared to other professors. AVOID!

5-minute 8 AM quizzes every Thursday on complex topics such as convolution and Fourier series computation. Encouraged us to come to his office with questions, and then said he couldn't help when I actually went. Very rarely gave a clear answer to any of my questions, and assigned 60+ question homeworks weekly. He is a very generous grader, however.

He encouraged us to come to his office hours if we had questions, but whenever I went for homework help he told me that he couldn't help me or even tell me whether my approach was correct. Homeworks were incredibly long (60+ questions) and due twice a week. I might would have failed if not for the TA; shout-out to my man Wasif. Take Lanzerotti.

A bad professor, but does not deserve the rating he has here. Had him for signals. Lectures are suboptimally delivered, there are two homeworks per week , and on top of that in-class quizzes at 8 AM that your grade depends on. For the last lab we were expected to know MATLAB even though it was not mentioned once before. Get Lanzerotti.

Long and difficult homeworks (over 100+ canvas questions) with mistakes and concepts not on exams, mandatory quizzes every class that are difficult and unhelpful and weighed alot towards your grade, lectures were okay but not enough to understand material, and relied on lanzerotti for exam reviews and even office hour assistance.

Prefacing this by saying that I didn't take the same class as any of the other reviewers. Intro to Opto is where prof. Xu shines, because he is teaching people who have already taken the basics of Electrical Engineering. That being said, homeworks became repetitive and lectures too. Otherwise, fairly easy course if you could stay awake.

I had prof Xu for the spring 2024 semester. Honestly, my review wouldn't be as bad as it is if it weren't for Dr. Lanzerotti. I wasn't even in her class section and she welcomed me to her office hours by first name and a breakfast bar whereas Professor Xu had one office hour on a very busy class time making it impossible for me to meet with him.

Xu gives 5 minute in-class quizzes that weighs 12% and sometimes difficult and impossible to finish in 5 mins. His slides were pretty much useless, hw's are ridiculously hard and always falls behind other classes. Also a research prof required to "teach" so he doesn't care about teaching and makes alot mistakes when grading or when making his hw's

Had him for ECE 2214 and 2714, Worst professor for ECE. He is never prepared for class and makes mistakes with assigning quizzes/hw. For 2714 Hw's I would spend upwards to 9 hrs. He changes his slides from the original leaving off good examples. Assigns quizzes every class period for attendance. I essentially had to learn everything on my own.

Took ECE 2714 with this professor and it was a disaster. The material was  difficult and he complicated things a lot. He doesn't grade anything for the class and gets the other professor to do it or his TAs; labs, exams and quizzes. He assigned a quiz every morning for the 8am class. Learned everything on my own. I would choose Dr. Lanzeroiti.

Honestly this might be unpopular but I think this guy is over-hated. He's not an outstanding lecturer but the examples are relatively helpful if you pay attention. Homeworks are fine, kind of long but fairly similar to the tests. Circuits is just a pretty tough class in general but I don't think he's as outstandingly bad as his other ratings imply.

I literarily could not believe how bad of a professor he is. I had him last spring and while I passed with a decent grade, it was 100% because of YouTube. There is absolutely no reason to go to class, he gets mad if you ask questions. Show up 10 minutes before the end of class to be there for the quiz, I wish I had. He has no interest in teaching.
Lectures were confusing and hard to follow. Professor was not able to give clear answers to questions in class. His powerpoints had good information and examples but you will have to teach yourself.

If you ask him a question in class he will either defer to a TA or will stammer for a minute without answering. He also will spend days on the exact same problem without changing anything. Lecture slides rarely are helpful for assignments. Graded assignments never have feedback and partial credit is rarely given.

This professor was awful, I watched another student in his class ask a question about a topic they didn't understand and this professor straight out denied him an answer and said something to the tune of "no, I don't have time for that". By the end less than 1/2 the class was showing up to lecture because it didn't do anything.

Terrible professor. Changed our grading policy the week before finals. Doesn't answer questions fully, skims across subjects without stopping to take any questions, and expects everyone to have previous knowledge of electrical circuits. If you're in ME, you might have to take this guy because he's the only one that teaches the class, so good luck.

The tests are graded with a very clear rubric for credit/partial credit which seems great in theory but the graders deviate from it at will and then refuse to explain their reasoning for it. There aren't many labs but they can be time intensive and again, grading is erratic at best- I received grades from a 65 to a 99 with the same quality of work.

He is entirely incompetent as a teacher. His lectures are almost impossible to follow and typically vastly overcomplicate what should be simple topics. Tests are typically harder than the homework and are graded very harshly. Small errors such as dropping a sign or writing a number wrong will cost you up to 10 points on a problem.

One day he literally did the same example over and over (no difference in the way he did it). Also the content we were learning was like three weeks ahead of what we were being quizzed and tested on. For homework, there were worksheets with diagrams and they didn't match the canvas quiz, so you just had to guess what he was actually asking.

Your grade in this class depends entirely what TA grades your work. Some give generous partial credit and some give almost none which in his class is the difference between a 30% and a 70%. Yong Xu himself is a terrible lecturer and takes no responsibility for his TA's actions, telling students to bring concerns to TAs.

Xus tests are reasonable and based on what he covers so if you put in the time, you can get at least a C or B. I recommend him over the other ECE professors because he actually teaches and is fair. I took this with Lu and failed because Lu did not teach the material on his tests, but did fine in Xus class.

Unclear is the word for this professor, he told us that we would be unable to even ball park our grade before the last day I decide to withdraw or not. Unclear and unable to understand his lectures. Exams and quizzes are you know it or you fail it. I've had worst professors at teaching, but at least I knew where I stoof in the class.

I'm not actually sure what Xu is doing with my grade. He has released the final and said that HE doesn't know what our grade is. If you can, take this class with anyone else but Xu. The final exam is much harder than anything I've ever seen. It's like cooking a pizza and just throwing EVERYTHING at the plate and hoping it works.
Extremely confusing, the only way you will learn is if you use the textbook. Half the class is expected to have to take it again.

This class is a project-based class where you and one other partner make one of four provided projects. Professor Yu does a decent job steering you in the right direction if you ask questions, but it really is an independent class. He's alright and gives decent advice, but ultimately, you and your partner are in charge of your project.

Descent IDP professor. He's an easy grader. Unfortunately, many IDP professors grades based on the figures/pictures...He gave feedback when necessary, and helped steer my project in the right direction. The TAs for Home Audio this semester were really good too-they gave me the most help. Your experience is kinda a gamble on who your partner is....
Great professor and detailed lecturer. Homework assignments were relevant and helped prepare me for tests.

Very nice guy, didn't really like his lectures. I felt he didn't really teach anything, he would just restate lecture slides. I did well in the course by going to office hours every week and doing HWs and labs there. Very lenient grader, does a lot of error care to make sure you get max amount of points.

Not bad. We had the highest test averages compared to the other professors. Tries to joke but they often fall flat. Pretty lenient grader, but made mistakes on grading and answer keys (mightve been ta issue, not sure) so make sure to double check stuff.

Good professor. Homework was reasonable, and lectures were well thought out. Yu provides a lot of study material, such as review slides and exams from previous years, which helps with studying for exams.  Make sure to take advantage of ULA and GTA office hours, as I found those extremely helpful when completing homework and labs.
He is a cool guy. Lectures can be better but generous grader overall.

Make sure to attend his lectures as this class is lecture heavy. His personal website contains lots of solved practice problems that add to the lectures.  The class material is only as difficult as it is due to the material being covered. He does his best to make it easier. Yu does his best to give back points and extend assignments when he can.

Professor Yu is alright. Nothing special really. This class is really easy and honestly really interesting. There is a lot of different things you can learn from it and he gives feedback on the labs to help you with your writing.

I absolute loved this class- it's a very easy pathway and the content was super interesting! Duma is great at going into detailed explanations on the topics, and as long as you pay attention to the end-of-chapter quizzes every week, the final cumulative quiz is pretty easy. Highly recommend!
If I had to describe his classes as a sauce, I'd say they're awesome sauce.
Amazing. If you need an easy pathway, just take this one. It's interesting too.

I really liked this class, it was very easy and I didn't need to go to the class to do any of the assignments. There are two online open note quizzes each week and the final is open note too. Dr. Duma was really kind, had engaging lectures, and was helpful.

ugh i loved this class. just two quizzes a week (some mini assignments here and there) and the lectures have all the answers. the content was really interesting and the website used was very engaging and easy to navigate. it just sucks u have to pay so much for the program. i'm taking the new helmet designs course next sem too!
This class is super cool and has an awesome online textbook. Apparently he is also making a new class with a similar textbook that counts for a 3 and 7 pathway.

Took the class in person this past spring and it was super nice. Quizzes were straightforward since Dr. Duma marks what exactly is tested from each class. Take this class if you need an easy A or to fulfill a pathway!!! Can't recommend this class enough. Course is organized well so you know what will be tested and don't need to waste your time studying random stuff. Course material is also interesting if you like the content. Take the class!!

I had Dr. Duma for concussion perspectives and absolutely loved it! I was talking to him after class and he told me about a new class he's creating for spring 2024. This class was absolutely flippin fantastic. This man carries the virginia tech curriculum on his back. I highly recommend.

This has been one of my favorite classes I've taken at VT. The material is really interesting, and Dr. Duma has cool stories incorporated into each lecture. Definitely take this class before you graduate!
My favorite class at Virginia Tech! He covers a great deal of material, but you know what to study and the exams are not hard. Also, there are many options for extra credit.
Professor Duma has an abundance of knowledge and his class shows it. This class really is a hidden gem at Virginia Tech.
Best Pathways 1 and 4 class, I recommend students take this fun and interesting class. Lots of funny jokes worked into each lecture.
The best Pathways class I have ever taken. You will LOVE the class, great teacher, and the concussion material is fascinating.
Excellent professor, great class, learned so much about concussions and science. I recommend this class to everyone. So much of the research actually took place at Virginia Tech.
Amazing professor and class. Everyone should take this class. Extra credit really helps.

Easiest class you will take at Virginia Tech. Attendance is not mandatory but the subject matter is interesting which makes class enjoyable! Everything on the exams is clearly marked and there is so much extra credit, it's hard not to get an A in this class. Highly recommend for a pathway!

Really good class and has interesting topics. Dr. Duma is a great guy and loves what he teaches. Take this class, and if you do the extra credit and pay attention class you will get an A. What a great class!!
Literally anything you'll be tested on is clearly indicated on presentation slides. Incredibly easy A, I have shown up 4 times and got an A with ease.

Took this asynchronously in Fall 2022. He does this in-person in Spring, and online in Fall from what I remember. Everything about this class is amazing for someone who loves to work ahead! Super understanding professor, and information is very clearly marked when needed to know for exams. Tons of opportunities for extra credit.
This was a very easy class. I currently have a 106 because there's a lot of extra credit. He puts checkmarks next to the information you need to know. The material is also interesting.
The class was asynchronous, but everything was clearly communicated. Powerpoints outline what is important for exams. Lots of extra credit. Professor was nice and understanding.

One of my favorite courses! He makes the material very interesting and easy to understand. The workload was very light and he lets you do it at your own pace. Offers multiple extra credit assignments and highlights the information on the power points that might be on the exam.

Professor Duma's class was so enjoyable for me. His lectures were intriguing, and he provides clear expectations of what is to be known for the exams.
