Great professor- made it easy for you to get a good grade and the lectures are clear and include interesting material!
This is an absolutely amazing professor. I had him for Concussion Perspectives and it really was an easy A. He is very generous with extra credit and will sometimes give out candy :)
Pretty good
Pretty easy professor, TAs do all the grading. A little bit confusing and unorganized but the class is easy so it doesn't matter. Would take again.

Doesn't teach at all and relies entirely on the TA's for grading and teaching. Virtually impossible to get a timly reply on an email or assignmetn comment. The grade weighting between assignments makes no sense. Some tank your grade while some do nothing for it
She was chill. TAs did all the grading. Attendance was required I think? they were kind of unclear about it. Overall, easy class.

Really nice professor. Most of the assignments are group work and aren't very difficult. Her and the TAs grade pretty easy and want you to succeed. She also added multiple extra credit opportunities to help boost people's grades and encourage them to come to class.
Nice woman, very easy class if you get a good group
Class was as expected, but two group members completely left us in the dust and the professor didn't seem to care until I sent an email containing undeniable proof.
Very kind professor who is pretty flexible and understanding, they "count" attendance with name tags but if you miss a couple classes you can make it up.
It's mostly group projects, so if you do them you should pass the class. She is a really nice teacher.
She is just a great person and it is fun to be in her class.
She is a very nice professor; if you do the work, you should pass

This guy was amazing for Multi. He explained stuff so well and really put time into each lecture. He used Desmos and 3D graphing material in class to explain the difficult concepts and his tests were relatively easy as long as you do the practice tests. I definitely recommend him!

Dr. Hicks is good about rephrasing his questions until his students understand what he is asking. He is not afraid of long silences and will wait until someone has an answer. Love this professor 10/10! Made math understandable and even offers to replace a midterm exam grade with the final exam grade at the end of the semester:) Offers lots of help and guidance and is very patient! He is just genuinely a very good professor props to him truly.

Great math professor- quite rare here. Can't say much about his grading in particular because the class was standardized but I found it easy. He WILL know your name if you come to class. Would take a class with him again in a heartbeat.

Matthew James was a good professor. The class required you show up for part of the semester (where attendance was taken), but he's amendable to that! The whole class is basically working on a group design project. Its as easy as FYE classes get. Prof. is very nice and easy to talk to. You have to write reports and eventually complete a big project but its very manageable.

Matt is a really good professor who cares about his students' well-being. The class is mostly group projects, but he and his TAs grade easily and want the class to succeed. I found the Matlab and CAD he taught quite easy to understand. He grades pretty easily, too, and getting an A is very easy as long as you work with your team and get things done on time.

Great teacher! Prof. Matts's lectures were always engaging and he made time to help on difficult assignments. The class is centered around group work but Prof. Matt makes sure that each teammate is doing their part so that everyone participates which makes the activities much easier to do. Would love to have as a teacher again!

Matt James the goat. Great professor, cares about his students a lot and is very understanding. Attendance started to become mandatory towards the end of the semester. I love this man so much. He is so understanding and caring and has a grace period for all assignments. He is very lenient with extensions and genuinely cares about his students. Group projects are actually fun and fairly laid back. Please please please take a class with THE Matthew James.

THE Matt James was an amazing professor for 1414. He was super caring and while some assignments were a bit of work/writing the grace period he provides students as well as his flexibility when it came to extended deadlines was definitely helpful.
Grace period 🙏 Nice person, great professor.

Professor James really cares about his students. He is extremely laid back and will give out extensions like they are candy. Assignments take only a little bit of effort, but he is a lenient grader and it's almost impossible to not get an A. The group project is pretty easy as long as you get along with your team. Matt will give you great feedback.

Matt was an amazing professor. I would recommend him to anyone taking ENGE 1414. He truly cares about his students and is extremely supportive. As long as you complete your assignments with effort you will do great in the class. He is very lenient and understanding when it comes to late assignments if you tell him beforehand.
As long as you go to class and put a bit of effort into the assignments the class is easy. Hardest part was getting along with some group members

Matt is a great professor for the Foundations of Engineering class. Even though the lectures are somewhat lengthy, they fly by because of the variety in each class. Most of the semester is spent doing something completely different from the last week, which makes for an interesting class.
was a great teacher, material and lectures were a bit boring but he does care about his students and is quite lenient as long as you email him with any troubles

Professor James is very knowledgeable on the subject. While you can expect to put a lot of time into homework and group work, his grading is very forgiving, and his feedback is very helpful. He is extremely kind and approachable, so expect to pass with flying colors if you put in the effort.
Class is kind of annoying and boring, but Matt is great and is a pretty easy grader. Just put effort into the work and you will get an A. Having a good team also helps a lot.
Lots of tedious but easy work. Easy class.

Basically a completion grade. Do the work by following the rubrics to get an A. It is one big group project that you work the whole semester towards. Matt is very understanding and grants extensions if you ask early enough. Respects students and tries to make our lives easier and not unnecessarily harder.

matt is the best!! he is very open and very good at communicating with the class. he cares about what you have to say and will actually listen to you. he is also younger than some of the other profs for 1216, or at least it seems that way, so its fun to joke around with him. even though the class was at 9:30 am, matt made me want to go

Truly a great professor, Matt cares about his students and gives meaningful feedback. He worked for many years as a civil engineer and is an expert in the field. He was always pretty easy-going and supportive when it came to the project. Was very approachable and always tried to help and talk if we needed it. Definitely recommended for the engineering foundations class.

Overall he was a good professor. Assignments were graded exactly based off rubrics. He is also very helpful if you want to sit down with someone about choosing a discipline(will sit down himself or find someone for you to talk too, especially if you are interested in civil engineering).

A well-rounded professor that makes the course tolerable for those going into General Engineering. Attendance is encouraged, but are not mandatory. He's pretty understandable with circumstances in which you are unable to attend (e.g. overslept, colds, etc.) and overall, is very resourceful and delivers the lectures well in a proficient manner.

Class is easy itself, but he is a great professor who cares about his students and wants them to receive As. Gives good feedback on team reports and MATLAB assignments. Very reachable and responds quickly. Makes students do cool poster board sessions instead of being in front of class for presentations which was unique. Overall great and easy.
He gives great feedback and is always willing to help. Even though going to class is sometimes hard, you should. He gives a lot of in class time to get work done which is very helpful.

Super accommodating, fun, sweet professor. Definitely my favorite so far. The assignments can be tedious for the class as a whole, but they're not hard at all. No exams or really even presentations (just poster sessions). Get him if you can; I can tell he likes each of his students as an individual and is looking out for us.
While I am not a massive fan of this course's material, Prof. James made the class interesting and engaging. I would highly recommend him for any general engineering course, especially 1414.
definitely try to get him if you can

Instead of presentations in front of the class for our group projects, everyone just did poster sessions, which really took the pressure off. Prof James was a great professor. He is understanding about due dates and assignment due dates if you contact him in advance. I loved his teaching style. This guy was in the engineering field before he became a professor, so his lectures and assignments are very structured. Read everything carefully, put quality work, and you'll get an A.

Professor James was so nice and always eager to help his students. Enge 1215 and 1216 are not too difficult in terms of curriculum, so a good professor can make or break that class. Prof James had great TAs and his grading criteria was always thoroughly explained ahead of the project.

Professor James is an awesome professor! This semester we did a group design project which was so fun because we were allowed to pick what we worked on! The class is really easy as long as you get a good group to work with.

Easily one of the best ENGE education professors. He's very flexible with students and meeting their needs, as well as adjusts his schedules according to what we need. The projects are very straightforward and he has clear grading rubrics. Not to mention he is personable and funny. Highly recommend.
Great dude. Clearly cares for his students. The curriculum is a little boring but he tries to make it as painless as possible.

Professor James is a good teacher. He is very nice, knowledgeable, and easy to talk to/reason with. He offers extensions if you need one, but you probably won't because there is not a lot of work in this class. It is mainly a semester-long series of group projects with assigned members. Class time is interesting and the material/projects are easy.

I had Matt for both ENGE 1215 & 1216 (by choice). He is a great professor, and he really cares about his students. While he can be a tough grader, he provides clear criteria for each assignment. Matt understands how heavy your workload can get throughout the semester and will help to work around it if you just tell him. Don't be afraid to ask him questions, he's willing to help. Best professor I had my freshman year.
Great Professor easy to work with learns his class

Matthew James is a good professor to have for Foundations of Engineering. He teaches everything you need to know and provides feedback for each assignment. Great professor, would definitely recommend taking him!
Good guy and teacher. Not the easiest grader, but will help you out if you ask for it.

James was a really great guy, he made this class really enjoyable. He knew a lot about applicable engineering jobs and projects so that was really nice. Great Teacher

Matt is great. By far one of my favorite teachers so far. He's a good teacher and makes the class as interesting as he can. He's also really nice and approachable and he truly cares for his students. James is a good professor to take for foundations. Lectures are as interesting as the preset course allows. Group projects are given with enough time and gives good feedback. Pretty solid teacher for Foundations of Engineering during your first semester. The whole course itself is a pain, and he attempts to make it less painful. The class itself is very easy so it wasn't a problem, but she's not an especially good grader.

lowkey dont know what these people are talking about. She's pretty good, I get the tough grading part, but she's not that strict as long as you follow the criteria. Pretty chill and attendance was only mandatory for two classes.

lectures are useless, spends the majority of time talking about things that do not help you learn and wastes incredible amounts of time, worth showing up to class to meet with your team but that's about it

Class is awful and pointless. You can learn everything taught online and not in the hour and fifteen minutes that is wasted from your day. Grades insanely hard for no reason.

This rating really reflects more on the 1215/1216 program than Professor Van Tyne herself. She is a bit less enthusiastic than other professors. This is mainly due to her HORRIBLE project, which requires a lot less work but is a lot less rewarding in the end. If you get a bad group, good luck.

The previous reviews are highly accurate. This woman can not explain things at all. If I could change my afternoon class to 8 am for a better prof I would. Boringest lectures hard to stay awake. nothing is taught from the view of a first time learner.

Overall, the content of the class was horribly boring, but I don't think it was really her fault. She's a pretty direct teacher. She's boring and gives many assignments but depending on your skill is an easy A.
Very obviously doesn't know what she is doing, good thing I actually did know before taking this class.
It's a pointless class. They will still try to fail you though.
Her lectures were some of the worst I have seen at VT both in content and presentation. Horribly frustrating class ans Mrs Tyne made it much more so.

Not a very good professor. She's quite intelligent, and it definitely shows when she's teaching but, she can't teach. She confuses students by answering questions. He is one of the most neutral professor's I've ever had. CS 3114 is really just working on projects and the majority of the time the professor is not needed. Not accessible. Sullivan is a nice guy but is not a very good professor. His lectures are boring and random and I never learned anything from them. Overall, good professor. Has opt-in attendance that basically just adds 10% to your final grade. The lectures are boring and he gets derailed a lot, but nobody stops you from just not listening to him. He's easy to approach and ask questions, and I always left with a clear answer.

Professor Sullivan is very knowledgeable about 3114 topics and enjoys teaching. The lectures can be dry as is common with complex Computer Science courses. It's not entirely his fault. The only reason I got an A minus in this class is because I spent multiple hours a week in office hours asking the TA's for help.

He offers a lot of extra credit for submitting projects early which is nice but his lectures don't really teach you. Pick another professor if possible. Lectures are not helpful, he only talks about what he's passionate about and not really what you need to know, but you should go in case of random attendance checks.

Mr. Sullivan is good, he did mess up Project 1 somewhat for our semester but he did change some things after that and the rest of the course was fine. Professor uses webcat grading software with mutation testing implemented which was not explained and everyone didn't know how to use the software so the class averaged a 40  on the project and 35% dropped the class before the due date. Professor then said that we didn't work hard enough and how he won't be changing how the course is organized

Caring and kind professor. Needs more experience but he is young, so he is still learing. Stayed back many times to help students out. Even sacrificed spring break to help us with project 2. Enjoyed learning from him.

This is a tough class. You have to be willing to put extra effort and start projects early. However, Mr. Sullivan is a great and caring professor. He stayed back a lot of times as the project deadline approached to help the students out. He was personable and wants to become a better teacher.
Awful.
Avoid at all costs! Trust me, save yourself.
Bad, very very bad
You know it's bad when the other 3114 professor is changing her curriculum because Sullivan's project structure is unfair for students and TAs.
This is the most frustrating, unreasonable, mismanaged class I have ever taken.

Never responsive outside of class, piazza and email responses are very slow or otherwise get completely ghosted. Project instructions are a bit confusing. The only positive thing is the 10% extra credit for projects.

Professor Sullivan is a very knowledgeable and very passionate professor when it comes to CS 3114. He gives 10% extra if you turned in the project 2 days early which carried my grade A LOT. Beware of the occasional pop quizzes he gives for attendance.

Dr. Baumann is one of the smartest professors I've had so far. Very strict grader, but seemed to ease up later in the semester. He goes through each report fully, leaving detailed and constructive criticism. Would 100% recommend if you care more about learning than your grade.

Could you take another professor and get a higher grade way easier? Definitely. Baumann is a smart guy though and never fails to crack jokes, he is one of the few ECE professors who genuinely cares about his students and makes class interesting.

Had for AC and Analog Lab. Very challenging labs and finals. Useful and interesting; really got the hang of EE because labs required intuitive and mathematic understanding - one of the few professors that provided both thoroughly. Did not always provide enough material to get started. 20 hours design, 5 minutes building. very witty.

2804 is a semester long project class. If you put in the work, he will explain anything you need help with. Getting A's on weekly reports requires it to be 'impressive.' This can be that you made great progress, included something he hadn't seen before, had good conclusions etc, but he has to like your report better than others, else get a B, max.

Professor Baumann is a nice guy but a hard grader. Doing your reports with everything working will get you an 80%. He only gives A's to students that go above and beyond. He is really good at explaining things and helping you fix problems. I'd recommend him for 2804.

If you show up to class, take notes, and study, you'll be fine. Dr. Madigan made sure to give students everything they needed to fully understand the material. Avoid missing lectures as pop quizzes sometimes occur at the end of class.
No no no. Do not take him.

If there was any other option I would take it in a heart beat. He is all lectures, random pop quizzes and 0 accommodation. He picks favorites, tries to intimidate and is not at all nice. Trying to be funny but is rude and grades very harsh. Should another teacher teach this course I'd advise you choose them.

He will not lower standards but he will do everything he can to help you reach that standard and he keeps his word. He will help you whenever you need it. You cannot skip his class because parts of the note will be filled in during class. One of the best professors in ISE and he makes every effort to ensure that you understand the material and why.

Dr. Madigan is literally the best. Try to avoid missing lectures because all of the test and quizzes are based off of the lecture notes. TAs can be hard graders, but if something is really off Dr. Madigan will typically hear out your argument

Very frustrating professor. Smug and condescending at times. Moreover, the grading on the tests is entirely unfair. You will get a 20% or a 100% on the exams, as they rely on an autograder. No extensions/extra credit even for valid cases.  Important to mention: 95% of the learning comes from the assignments. 60% of the class skips lectures

Pretty good professor for someone without any C++ experience. Lectures are generally pretty good. He didn't prepare us well for the first midterm, but did a great job preparing us for the second one and the final. The projects can be tricky, but you can usually manage on your own.

ECE 2514 is a horrendously run class, I do not think it is entirely the professor's fault but the class sucks. Lectures aren't really helpful, and the midterm exams are very poorly run. I am pretty sure this professor is the best of the three, but it doesn't really matter much because you have to learn this course all by yourself.

They made the class a lot harder this past semester, so for a first time coder it was pretty difficult. I failed the first exam and I initially blamed him for lack of teaching. However, I met with him multiple times outside of his office hours to relearn concepts I didn't understand in class. Doing that and taking good notes shot my grade back up.

Half the class failed the midterm, and this was arguably the professors fault, as he even admitted that we should have been taught the material via a different method. This class is a cakewalk if you already understand C++, if not, it's better to learn it on your own than to pay attention to his lectures. Attendance rarely made a difference.

Soysal is entertaining and gives helpful analogies for people who haven't coded before. The class isn't terrible although most of the averages seem to be 50's since half the class doesn't know anything and the other half has coded before. If you wanna pass, just do the assignments... don't use chatgpt (half the class failed the midterm).

Alkan Soysal doesn't know how to teach people how to code. The assignments in the course were poorly made, often having mistakes or requiring students to do things in the wrong way only to then cause students problems because they did it in the wrong way. This doesn't help the students learn better, it just adds a lot of confusion and extra work.
Knows what he's doing and tries his best to make sure everyone in his lectures does too.

Dr. Soysal is an awesome professor. This was my first forte into coding, and after doing poorly on the midterm exam (yes ik it was easy, I improved a lot over the last 8 weeks), he very much helped me get back on the right track. Take him if you have the chance, you won't regret it!

Dr. Soysal is a very accessible and often funny professor, while most people in this class have already had coding experience or something similar Professor Soysal works hard to add onto topics and match the rigor of the class with input from the students(if they ever speak up haha)

The lectures for this course were very interesting and engaging. However, the grading system could use some work. The exams are very difficult and long. It would be nice to have more extra credit opportunities to help with the grade. Class supports naturally talented ones. Hard work did not help me.

He is a great teacher and a really nice/caring guy. He wants you to succeed and will help you if you go to him. In general, it is a difficult class and exams are hard but the more you go to office hours and get help, the better you will do.
Very clear at teaching. Would recommend, but can make the fluid lab difficult than other sections.

No grades homework, only chapter quizzes and exams. Definitely the better option than Scardina if you're trying to get a decent grade. Still a difficult class, but at least you have a chance with this prof.

Homework is optional so the class grade is essentially composed of exam grades. 4 exams (lowest dropped) + final exam. The homework is great practice for the exams and the recitation sessions are exremely useful. If you study these, you should do fine on the exams. This prof also makes the class fun and is far less terrifying than Scardina.
She is kind and does her best to be helpful, but the lectures can be pretty boring... partially due to the material though.

Prof. Senger is a very good lecturer, so make sure to take good notes. Homeworks help your understanding and determine a lot of the grade, but make sure you go to office hours! You won't understand the content without it. Take initiative (office hours) if you don't understand something--the course content is very weird and you can get lost easily.

Very kind professor. Her lectures are very boring, but if you lock in and take notes, they are very useful for the projects and exams at least in my experience. I will say that there were a lot of delays with assignment releases and grading. I don't think she is as bad as some of the reviews say, but definetly not the best.

Senger is one of the better 1114 professors. Considering 1114 is a weed-out class, it will be difficult, but Prof. Senger tries her best to make it as easy as possible. The work is a little difficult but the lectures and reading the course help a lot. I would consider her the best prof. for 1114 (def not Edwards)
Much better than the other CS 1114 professors especially Edwards. She is very caring and understanding to any life circumstances. Her lectures are also informative as far as lectures go.

REALLY GREAT PROFESSOR! Senger gives amazing advice and can answer EVERY question even the most poorly worded CS questions. CS 1114 is tough, but her office hours are a lifesaver! Her lectures are awesome, and she's so sweet. She's the perfect professor for this class and she's never condescending.

Professor herself was very nice. Lectures aren't required but may be helpful if you just started programming. The course itself is difficult because it's a weed-out class. The main content of the class is from the weekly readings, lectures are just a bonus if you need more help. Labs are okay but the later programs are what kill people.

She's a fine professor, she is passionate but the course was created by Dr. Edwards and it is not a good course. CS 1114 is not a good course that is supposed to be an introductory course but what a lot of your grade counts for is not helpful to your learning.

Time consuming projects, bad queues, weren't given project 1 for a month or 2 and after that it all snowballed, we only had a week for Project 4 binary bomb.  Midterm and final avg really low too along with final exam, barely any curve. Professor made too many excuses during lecture on why something wasn't uploaded yet, all around unfun experience.

She was an amazing teacher for CS1114 when I took her but for CS2505 I will never ever suggest her. I dont think anything in the lectures that were taught to us was used in the projects or the tests that we were expected to get good grades on. Everything is super hard in the class when its Professor Senger!!!

She barely graded anything until the last two weeks of the semester, so you didn't know your actual grade until the last week of the semester. The final was impossibly hard, and tanked my grade a whole 10%. Material on the final was barely anything covered in the lectures. Barely gives usable feedback, and so boring in lecture.

First of all this class is extremely difficult for many people that have never coded before and the course is designed to mostly be self-taught.  However, Allyson tries her best to explain what is in the reading activities during 45 minutes of lecture time in a clear and understandable way.  She is also a very nice and friendly person.

I really enjoyed having her! Her lectures explained concepts clearly, and I could tell that she enjoyed teaching. She's really nice, which is a breath of fresh air in the CS department. Also, she wasn't condescending when I asked her questions and would thoroughly explain her answers, so it made her seem very approachable. Highly recommend!

For lectures she read the weekly readings we needed to do ourselves to the class, so I got by teaching myself the material. The quizzes were heavily weighted for this class, although I don't think they're an accurate measurement of one's ability to write code or understand this class's content.

Senior design continues from fall and will be the most demanding yet rewarding semester with a lot of team meetings. Teams meet weekly with Dr. Shinpaugh. LISTEN to his advice and make solid slides for him to review. Know your Concept of Operations. Major deliverables include ABET, standards, poster, final report, and presentation. Good luck!!

Dr. Shinpaugh is incredibly smart and knows what he's talking about. Despite this, he's not great at teaching introductory topics. He essentially assumes you already know the basics of electronics. The class isn't too hard as long as you work at it, but you'll need to put in a lot of effort on your own if you want to understand the material.

Honestly he was alright. He was very nice but it was his first time teaching and you can tell he doesn't know how to teach. He taught the first half not too bad but the second half made no sense at all. He let us take our tests at home because the desks were small so pray for small desks. He doesn't help well with homework so make friends!

Dr. Shinpaugh is kind but a bad professor. To succeed in this class, rely heavily on the textbook, as the lectures don't align well with the tests. The tests cover random material from class but are open book. Labs are easy, and homework is time-consuming. Be prepared to study on your own to get a good grade bc his office hours are not helpful.

Senior design starts with lectures on systems engineering and models, followed by an orbital debris report. Some weekly meetings with Dr. Shinpaugh may be unhelpful, ASK QUESTIONS! Review past team reports to understand expectations. Final work includes a ~50 page report (50% of grade) and ~45 minute presentation. Work is challenging yet rewarding.

I did well in this class, but no thanks to him. Tries to be relatable to students but just misses the mark completely. The amount of smartbook assignments we had was ridiculous. Caring guy in person but incoherent lecture slides(bad handwriting). I learned more from my friends than from his lectures.Covered topics then tested them the next day.
This was my least favorite class all year. His way of teaching just takes the fun out of learning. Not entirely sure if I learned anything useful all year.

Shinpaugh is the case of a professor who is a great guy but can't teach for his life. His lectures are hard to understand and don't get me started on his handwriting. Some of his office hours are also hard to get to because they are far from campus. His saving grace is he makes his tests take home. I chose aero instead of electrical for a reason.

Lectures are awful, as the teacher cannot write anything legible. He doesn't explain concepts well at all and basically leave everything to the textbook, which is itself book that should go up in flames. Text book does nothing to actually teach and has only added to my confusion in this course. Prepare for the worst class you have ever taken.

Dr. Shinpaugh is caring and tries to help, but he winged teaching the course. Some content wasn't easy to initially grasp. Was ok at lecturing with terrible handwriting and poor class management. Test 1 had a low average, so he made other two exams and final more reasonable. Gave two extra credit opportunities to help students out.

Sometimes I think he makes decisions on how to run his class based on the direction the wind is blowing that day, or something else as arbitrary. He didn't even know the format of his own final by the last day of class. Poor handwriting, and he scrawls it on the margins of the slideshow. Tends to ramble about the space shuttle. Nice guy, though.

Lectures were hard to follow (mostly because of his bad handwriting) and homework/test averages were about what you would expect from a 2nd year engineering class, low. Tests were multiple choice. He may not have explained things super well the first time around, but if you asked him questions in or out of class he'd give you a better answer.

His handwriting is absolutely atrocious and illegible. His lectures were hard to follow and he was often wrong when going over examples. Only reason I learned anything was because of the lab supervisor (Not the TA). He is a nice guy though and did make himself available for questions (not that it helped). Good luck teaching yourself material!
The professor clearly did not know the material any better than the students. Teaching was bad. Homeworks and tests were all worded very poorly.  Avoid this professor!

Horrid teaching! He definitely was learning the notes while teaching them. He ignores emails with most homework questions. He just says to come to his limited office hours(had other classes during) Bad teaching and bad environment. He's my academic advisor that ignored my advising emails. Had to switch advisors so I could actually get advising help

Horrid, Horrid course. If you value your grade, then you will do well to NOT take any course with this guy. BTW OH was not recorded. Absolutely horrible.

Lectures don't help at all. She just repeats stuff you can easily find on Canvas and talks through the same things you already learning during the homework and in the labs. She's also unkind and unforgiving. Avoid having her if you can.
Lectures are mandatory even though you won't really learn anything. Just the same rinse and repeat practice problems which you will only get through 2

Lectures are useless. It's the same logistics over and over again, and vague hints for the weekly coding problems. The videos on Canvas by another professor are helpful, but it'd be way better if the material was taught in class rather than as an hour of homework. Professor Kiran is one of the more challenging professors I have had. The tests are worth 80%, and the homework is worth 20%. The tests can be difficult, and partial credit is rarely given. He told me my test grades were "below average," which is unprofessional and rude. He did boost my grade at the end because I showed up to office hours a lot.

A little slow-paced, but clear lectures and very doable tests. Can be a tough grader but fairly open to giving points back if you can show your reasoning. Can always improve your grade if you do better in later tests, even if you bombed a test.

10-question tests that are formatted in a way that sets you up for failure. Make 2 tiny mistakes? There goes your A for the class. Want partial credit? Welp, he doesn't believe in that. Oh, and if you get all questions right it won't guarantee a 100% bc if he doesn't like how you came to your answer you could get half credit (yes Im being serious).

Professor McDowell was one of the nicer professors I have had at VT. He was a bit difficult to learn from, but he got better as the semester went on (his first semester teaching separation processes). The TAs were a big help, as well as going to his office hours. The partial credit on exams was generous. The homework was tough to learn from.

Very sweet guy but cannot explain the material well. He knows the material very well but is bad at articulating it to students. He constantly makes mistakes during lecture and the practice tests have different material than the final. When I took this class, it was only his 2nd semester as an instructor, so take this review with a grain of salt.

Goes through lots of example problems, usually will take a problem straight off the slides or practice test for the test, which helps. However, he's not the best at explaining the concepts behind the math, which can make following the lectures difficult. Does provide extra credit/curve for all tests, which is helpful.

Gives substantial extra credit but doesn't waterfall which makes test grades feel like luck as small mistakes at the beginning can lead to -20 points. Somewhat boring lectures and can be hard to understand at first. On the other hand, he was accessible, provided valuable info and examples, and cared about student success, just ask him questions!

Practice tests are very similar to what is on the actual exams however I feel like he's a pretty tough grader for them, does try and help students during exams but can be misleading. Accent and handwriting can also make this difficult to understand during lecture

Dr. Aidi's lectures were somewhat hard to follow at times, but that's his only real downside. He's accessible outside of class, the homework isn't bad, the tests are similar to the practice tests and gives extra credit on each test. He runs through examples during class which can help but doesn't explain the concepts extremely well.

Aidi is quite boring during lecture and will run through practice problems without really explaining the concepts behind solving them. Gives tons of extra credit and is very clear about what content to expect on exams. Helpful during office hours. Overall very unique guy - he always seems like he's about to burst out laughing for some reason.

Aidi was very boring. I took his class from 5-6:15 and he wanted to leave just as much, if not more, than all of us. He just goes through the slides and you have to zoom along with him. Sometimes hard to understand his accent and handwriting. He grades pretty fairly on tests and gives extra credit for all of them.
Tough grader but curves in the end. Most tests are like his practice tests. In class he does go fast.

He did lots of examples in class, but he didn't explain the concepts. He solved problems in silence and asked if there were questions. He moves fast and doesn't care if the class understands. The tests aren't curved and is harder than the homework. The people who did well in his class, are the quick learners or who already understand the concepts.

Very cool guy. Always has this smirk on his face that's pretty funny. He gave me a deep understanding in Statics and is a good visual teacher. He also explains how the things we learn are going to affect us in deforms

Nice guy but seemed to explain everything in the most difficult possible way. He goes so fast and has high expectations. Very hard to learn from. My other friends in other statics classes learned way more than I did. I'd try to find another professor, but if you're stuck he won't make your life suck.
This class is very test heavy.  The majority of your grade is from all the tests.  If you are not a good test taker, good luck.  She is a hard grader as well.

She is a great professor and wants you to learn and succeed. If you ask questions she will help you. The class is difficult and very test-heavy but I feel like I learned a lot more than the people that look other sections of the class. She is very knowledgeable and knows her stuff.

You will likely get more out of this class with Prof. Behkam than other fluids classes because she genuinely wants you to learn the material. Entertains all questions (even irrelevant/distracting ones) which can sidetrack, however lectures are still good. Tests are hard, but all in all she is kind and truly wants you to become a good engineer.
I didn't take WGS2264. I took ME3414. She was excellent during lectures, very helpful in office hours, and fair when it came to grading.

Worst professor I have ever had. Tests alone are 84%of your grade and you will not pass her tests. She is horrible and goes so off topic during class then will tell u to focus. Tests are the worst thing in the world. Other class for fluids gets As on their tests as averages, the average on test 2 was a 24%.
Entertains all questions. For better or for worse.

This spring lab focuses on a team-based senior design project. Teams meet regularly with assigned TA and faculty advisor. There are also three meetings with the professor. Teams post weekly updates on Canvas and submit a final AIAA standard paper. There are no exams, and it's not too hard to earn an A with a solid project and consistent effort.

For it being Professor Davoudi's first time teaching Fluid Dynamics at Virginia Tech, he did his best to cover the material. He was constantly reassuring, inspirational, and caring about our success not just in the classroom but in life as well. He excelled at providing an engaging learning experience, often connecting theory to real life examples.

He is bad at: responding to emails, setting clear deadlines, controlling emotions, etc. Overall, be on his good side or you will know that you are not on that side. He is very unclear on the grading and deadlines. This is very important for project based classes, he does not send rubrics or deadlines dates until it is tooo late. Best of luck, GG

Dr. Davoudi is nice, but this lab was disorganized. After two labs, the schedule lacked structure. The 3rd lab, a foam glider project, felt like arts and crafts and pointless to report on. The 4th lab, satellite navigation, was scrapped. Graded on 3 lab reports and a senior design experiment with occasional meetings. Easy lab but poorly executed.

Prof Davoudi is a great guy,  but the structuring of this class was awful. The lectures consisted of him purely reading off of the slides and giving general equations. Never did ANY example problems and did NOT post his lecture notes. Constant issues with HW assignments. The tests were all in person and many of us felt grossly underprepared.

Dr. Davoudi is highly intelligent, and knows his material, but is apt to go on tangents and doesn't teach clearly. Most of my learning came from the textbook and other sources. He was also regularly late to classes, and asked us to stay late to make up for it. He's a great guy, but just be prepared to do the grunt work of learning on your own time.

Very nice man. Infuriatingly bad teacher. I learned about 25% of the course from him. Loves tangents. Loves curves. Loves extra credit. If you're planning on skipping every class, he's your go-to. I went to almost every class and it was a waste of my time.   My grade raised from a C to an A- from the final and extra credit.

You will either love or hate him. Does not work many example problems in class, and spends most of class going on rants and tangents, so be prepared to put in work outside of class. Curves every test, so your grade will be fine. I personally just didn't really care for his teaching style or his attitude.

100% would take his class again. HW took a long time but thats just bc the questions take a bit, not bc its a lot. He's a really kind prof. and you can tell he cares abt his students. Tests aren't too bad if you study and he curves heavy. He also helps w/ hw if you ask and responds quickly to emails. Plus his lectures aren't too boring for STEM.
Simple lectures and not to much homework (max two assignments a week). His test are hard, but he curves really well so it's totally fine. He's a really nice professor and explains the topics clearly.

First off you have to understand Statics is a hard course, anyone who had a bad review for Galitz just did not care enough to put effort into the class. Tests are heavily curved but there is a fair amount of homework. Has great lectures and is enthusiastic about what he's teaching. He does care about your grade but also that you learn the material.

Really amazing professor that wants to see you succeed inside and outside of the classroom. He talks through most lectures so you probably won't be taking too many notes. Try to understand the textbook homework as those concepts are translated to tests. Galitz gives you so many opportunities to make up your grade and learn from your mistakes.

Past reviews were misleading. His tests are different from homework and his curves are good but not enough for the difficulty of the exams. Studying for his tests is hard because you never know what to expect. He curves and gives extra credit but it was still a struggle to pass. In lectures, he talks about concepts instead of going over problems

He was a really great statics professor this year. He was always very understanding of students stress and made his lectures fun. The tests are hard but there's a big curve with every test. The class is very concept based and he doesn't work on very many example questions but he takes feedback very well and is helpful when you reach out.

You would have to try to fail Professor Galitz's class. His homework can be difficult, depending on the subject, but rarely is it overwhelming. His tests are very easy to score well on, as you can get 120/100 even before the curve, in which he curves the entire class to a median of 85/100. Take good notes, as you are allowed a cheat sheet on exams.
He was able to make 9am statics fun and engaging.  I didn't think that was possible. Highly recommend

Galitz is one of the most caring professors I have met. He deeply cares about a student's education and wants you to be successful. The course content can be difficult at times but he has safety nets for all the students so you don't have to worry about your grade. Attendance is not mandatory but you should definitely go anyways to learn.

He's definitely not the best lecturer I've had but he may be the most caring professor. He is genuinely passionate about try to teach students and works constantly to improve his teaching methods/materials. His exams are hard but they have large curves, expect to do poorly on the first one but don't freak out. Overall, solid professor.

Professor Galitz is very passionate about Deforms and he is always finding ways in improving his lectures. He is a very kind and generous man when it comes to test curves. He gives out massive test curves but his tests are very hard. Additionally, he also gives out extra credit opportunities. Not a lot of homeworks. Overall, a very good professor.

Dr. Galitz is easily the best professor I've had at my time at Tech so far. His eyes light up when talking about the material and he will happily answer any questions you have. He genuinely cares about teaching and he treats the class like he would his children, which includes disciplining them when necessary. Also gives out generous curves.
Galitz isn't the very best lecturer, I wish he would do more example problems in class, but his tests are very difficult with HUGE curves, so it is easy to succeed in his classes.

Nice guy and clearly passionate about the material. I wish there was less theory and discussion and more quantitative examples and math emphasis, but he did make an effort to make lectures entertaining which was appreciated. Generous curves and pretty quick homework assignments usually. Tests were definitely the hardest part but, again, big curves

His class is tough and test averages are usually low, but he explains what will be on each test clearly. He is a fair grader and what sets him apart is he grades on a curve that doesn't tank your GPA and actually reflects how you learned the material overall and compared to others in the class. Highly recommend him for statics

Professor Galitz cares about the success of his students. It is very possible to get a good grade in this class if you keep brushing over concepts you learn. If you are confused about something, put the effort and go to office hours. He is always ready to help and has office hours everyday!

Very down-to-earth professor that makes what could've easily been a boring and difficult topic into something intriguing. Tests are difficult but he will give you a chance to correct mistakes later on. Would recommend.

His teaching style isn't for everyone. He goes very deep into concepts, which I think confuses a lot of students, but if you go to class and ask him questions when you're confused, you will have a very good understanding of the subject. He genuinely wants you to do well, and offers good help during his office hours. Also, interesting guy to talk to

The only reason this guy is rated highly is because his curves are so generous he passes almost everyone in his class. He is not good at explaining the material and you will not leave his class with a good understanding of statics. If you don't need statics for future classes he's a good choice otherwise take it with another professor.

The tests are consistently hard. Thankfully the tests are all curved based on the results of the class, which can lead to a generous curve. Galitz is one of the best teachers I've ever met. He often cracks corny jokes in class and in-office hours will help you in a way to specifically make you understand. Once his student, always his student.

He curves each test so that the median is 85% - your grade will be fine. He tries to be motivational but just goes on tangents all the time and never fully works out problems so if you want to really learn statics/deforms take Chang or Davison. Hes not the worst and asks for feeback but he thinks he's better than he is so he doesn't really listen.

He's a horrible lecturer, doesn't work out problems, and just makes everything hard to explain. I had to teach a lot of the class to myself and the only reason anyone passes is because of his huge curves.

Many say that his exams are way too hard which is understandable but he curves majorly to make up for it. I got a 44 on the first exam for Statics and got curved to a 77 and after that I studied so much more and got at least a B+ on the rest of his exams including the final. Just study and put forth the effort he asks for and you will be just fine.

Dr. Seidel is an good professor for an 8 AM class. Intro to AOE is challenging but manageable. Great guy who is genuinely interested in what he teaches which makes lectures more engaging. Most kids stop showing up to lectures and those are the ones who fall behind. Seidel's class was incredibly difficult, easily being harder than the three credit hours it's worth. Gary is an absolute king. He offers tons of extra credit, keeps the highest score of your homework with unlimited attempts, and posts all his notes and videos of each lecture online. He is the best, treat him well and he will do the same to you, God bless this man.

Great guy who gives great lectures and ensures his students fully understand the material. Slides can be pretty dense though but very informative. This man is a genius and tells the best dad jokes. He teaches very tough subjects and expects a high amount from his students. His slides may be dense, but I don't think I could find another professor that could explain the subject as well as he does.

Fortunate enough to have Dr. Gray for both 1215 and 1216, saw a man with a mustache, thought he had to be cool.. and he was. Gave a great foundation for what it means to be a Hokie Engineer. Very funny professor who is accessible out of class as well. Had him for 1215 and 1216 and personally loved the way his class was run. 100% should take this professor's class.

Dull class, but Dr. Gray does a good job of giving you time to work with your team in class on your project. Most of the assignments can be done within 30 minutes. Gives funny shark facts every class and has an awesome mustache.

Dr. David Gray is one of the best professors at Virginia Tech. He will set you up for a lot of engineering related activities outside of his classes and provides a lot of support for both in class assignments and personal projects. Plus, his mustache is beyond peak.

Great professor; makes what is otherwise a tedious class entertaining and engaging. You are assigned a group for the entire semester, but he provides peer evaluations throughout the semester. Super fun professor. The entire premise of 1215 seems to be busy work, but I don't think that's his fault. Dr Gray is an amazing professor! His lectures are clear and fun. Dr. Gray is currently my favorite professor so far entering into Virginia Tech. I think he's a fun dude with a good sense of humor and takes things pretty easy. Amazing teacher that cares about making sure his students succeed in their careers. Pretty easy class as long as you do your work.

He is a great professor; he loves to use data to improve his teaching techniques. He is also hilarious and makes class fun. During the first 5 minutes of every class, he does a slideshow of collective funny things from the class before.

He has been the best professor/teacher I have ever had. If you can get him for your Enge section it is a must do. He was so good I even based my schedule for my next semester to be around the only 2 sections of the course he was teaching.
Immaculate Mustache. Really good dude.

Although I did struggle with the coding aspect of this course (which isnt too much) I enjoyed sitting in class for the hour and 15 since Dr. Gray made it interesting. Cool dude with the best mustache. He makes the class interesting even though the subject matter is not.
Gray is an amazing teacher, but your group really makes or breaks this class

Probably the greatest professor at Virginia Tech. He is hilarious, has amazing facial hair, and genuinely cares. Dr. Gray is an amazing professor, highly recommend taking his class. His lectures are very informative and pretty entertaining too. He has Platypus facts, and they are pretty humorous and a good way to start each class.

super nice guy, really funny, just a lot of busy work

Super funny guy, engaging lectures.  A lot of the assignments were tedious and the TA's graded a bit harsh for what the level of material.

Dr. Gray is super sarcastic and funny. He cares about his students and appreciates you for putting in effort. We had a lot of group work and a big group project so be sure to do your part in that. Overall, he's a fantastic guy!

very nice teacher, clear in her rubrics for projects. decent lectures, she is very knowledgeable. TAs were also very helpful. show up to class cause she made attendance mandatory at the end. communicate with your group and all will be fine.

Take her if you can. She is probably the sweetest professor on campus, and genuinely cares about her students. The work is also very easy. There is no reason you shouldn't receive an A in the class. Class is easy as long as you do your assignments. Prof. Dayoung is sweet & lenient, but is very quiet
The professor is kinda and help when asking questions. She is quite and hard to under sometimes.

Dr. Niko is super knowledgeable and passionate about the material in 2506. This is a heavily conceptual class. Professor Nikolopoulos knows his stuff, but with it comes some arrogance and irritation when students don't understand. His frustration while clarifying and answering some questions makes it hard to ask for help. It's difficult to learn without him but don't waste his time with your questions.

Very knowledgeable about the material. Overall, a decent professor in lecturing. Some concepts were confusing to understand. However, what makes him a 5/5 is how much he does outside of class. Discord office hours that cover most of the day, recorded in-class/supplemental lectures, and quick response times are great facets of the course.

He cares about what he teaches and is very passionate. He is also very liberal with extensions nowadays, and is willing to help you if you reach out. Also, he is incredibly knowledgeable about what he teaches.

Definitely a very knowledgeable instructor, the lectures were very in depth but sometimes were a bit confusing initially. Luckily all the lectures were recorded so you can watch it back. Piazza posts were very prompt and time for questions were available during the lectures. Homework was a bit heavy with the practicals but were helpful for quizzes.

Below average CS professor. Lectures are sometimes confusing and can go off on tangents unrelated to the course material. Doesn't really answer questions unless they are very specific and often times the answers to questions are unhelpful/ even more confusing.
A good teacher but not understanding of situations. A lot of lecture material you will have to learn yourself and there are not enough resources provided to learn yourself.

Dr. Nikolopoulos was a pretty great professor. Showed off his sense of humor from time to time and you could tell that he was very passionate about the course material. CS 2506 is a hard class but he makes it tolerable. Also, his response times on Piazza were 6 minutes at the latest.

Probably the best professor I've had at Tech. Super knowledgeable and explains things thoroughly and repeats concepts in the lectures so you gain a deep understanding of the subject matter. There is a lot of information you need to know in this class, but he puts in his effort, so you put in yours and you will be rewarded.
Professor is NOT willing to listen to you whatsoever. He is strict about stuff for no reason.

Prof nikolopoulos knows his stuff. He talks pretty fast during lectures but it's because he actually cares about what he's teaching and is excited. He explains everything in thorough detail so I never felt like I needed to ask questions during lectures. Definitely a hard class but he was always there to answer questions and cares about his students
Very nice proffesor. Wants his students to do well. Gives lots of chances for students to do well I just found the content not engaging. Little bit of a sleepy voice.

This professor has an incredibly vast and impressive knowledge of materials science. His powerpoint slides and lectures can be bland at times, but his clarity and anecdotes make up for it. Very easy class if you have any semblance of what type of questions will be on exams.

Great guy, he seems uptight at first, but turned out to be one of my favorite professors at Tech so far. He uses a lot of questions from the practice tests he gives, which is the bomb. There are usually two homework assignments a week based on text book questions. While reading isn't mandatory, I highly recommend it (it's my biggest regret).
Great professor. If you do the homework, study the practice tests, and read the textbook, you don't even need to go to class. I felt like I gained a lot from this class.

One of the best professors I have had so far in my educational journey at Tech! Definetly would take this course again, and  was one of if not the only class that I was excited to go to. Not attending class may result in 0s on assignments but he is very flexible with grades and late work. He is very nice and I would 110% recommend taking his class!

Mr. Bowen is a very cool teacher. He responded to emails in a timely manner which made it easy to for me to commuincate with him about assignments. He's pretty laid back and is flexible with deadlines as long as work is done and you show an intrest in the course by showing up.
Professor Bowen is an amazing professor, as well as person. He was able to make me WANT to go to class rather than have to go. His projects are fun and grading is lenient.

By the end of the semester, EVERY SINGLE STUDENT dropped the class except for one. Which was me. Unfair grading, no clear expectations, poor class layout. If you do not have to take this class for credit just don't take it at all.

The structure of this entire class was awful. Dr. Bohn does a terrible job explaining material, and rather just goes on tangents in class. Major assignments are given with not a sufficient enough time to complete, and there are multiple assignments due mostly every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Workload was too much for a 3 credit class.

The class was just bad all around. It could've been structured way better and there was an egregious amount of work given. Countless assignments that weren't necessary while more meaningful assignments weren't given enough time to be completed. It honestly felt like he thought we had nothing else going on besides his class and his assignments

One of the worst classes and professors I have ever taken at VT. In a semester with fluids, vibes, mech. design, and stats; this has been the most time consuming and worst class for everyone I know. The workload is completely unreasonable, the pacing of assignments is atrocious, the lecture are useless, and no partial credit on ridiculous exams.

I say attendance is mandatory half the time.  The professor is not at all understanding and comes across as not caring about his job as a professor due to his achieving tenure.  Extremely tough grader to an infuriating level.  Takes points off without fully giving a reason most of the time when it seems like it would otherwise receive full credit.

Fall 2020 covid semester ME3024. WHERE DO I START He was the worst teacher I've EVER had. Any of my classmates would agree. Just do yourself a favor and chose a different professor if you can. Horrible experience.

Dr. Bohn designed current ME3024. It is poorly written and teaches students to follow assignment rubrics verbatim instead of prioritizing understanding. One of the worst classes I have taken at VT. Him and his TAs grade really harshly. We get no partial credit on tests and quizzes. If you mess up a decimal, you lose all the points on the question. Jan Bohn is an awful professor. Lots and lots and lots of trailing off pointless assignments that do not add anything to the class. Hes a bad teacher. He trails off during lectures and makes a ton of bad jokes and gets frustrated when no one laughs. He doesnt help much.

Avoid if at all possible. His lectures are not helpful; he usually spends most of the time rambling about things barely related to the relevant topic. The first part of the course is newtonian mechanics, pretty easy. The latter two thirds of the course is about stability and control and is more challenging. There aren't many homeworks but they are annoyingly time consuming. The latter 2 exams are very difficult.

This was my lowest-performing class yet. I struggled after the first exam to keep up with the exam time requirements. While I feel I understood the material, I simply could not work fast enough. Joerger is a great professor who's funny and cares about his students. However, he had a hard time explaining alot of the concepts for the class clearly. This made some outside help essential to passing the class. Just the right amount of homework and ample extra credit with fast-paced tests not designed to be finished on time.

Joerger was a great professor. While his lectures could be hard to follow at times, we were always given a large amount of extra material to learn from, and all notes were uploaded. Homeworks and tests are designed to be very time consuming, but they are made fairly, and with ample extra credit built in. I would highly recommend Joerger!

Overall great professor with great lectures and he deeply cares about his students' success. Gives good extra credit even on exams which are designed to be VERY time consuming. Go to lecture to understand material better. Start homework assignments early since some take a while. Occasional take-home quizzes to test students on material. Cool class!

Wonderful professor!! I love Dr. B so much, definitely take her classes if you are able to! She is incredibly humble and is very caring towards her students. She sees the best in everyone, and will do her best to make you succeed. She is also incredibly interesting and fun, you'll love her! Wish I could take a class with her again.

Professor. Bairaktarova was very kind and caring toward her students. She would extend due dates if she felt the majority of the class wouldn't complete the assignment on time. There were no exams for ENGE 1216, only a semester-long project, where you had to build a tangible object and make a programming component.

Mainly go to class do in-class sketching for credit and homework is assigned weekly on an app. Very easy class and GPA booster. Just go to class to receive credit and do your work. A decent professor for a relatively easy course (Intro to Spatial Visualization). Homeworks were reasonable overall, though some were a bit difficult. The exams were difficult but solvable, and open-note. Having some experience in python/matlab/mathematica will make a lot of the homeworks and tests easier.

Lectures are hard to follow and monotonous. However, very clear notes and she does a few examples which helps a little. Lots of homework that was a tossup whether it was covered in class. Two AWFUL midterms harder than anything covered in class. The average raw for one of them was a 20. The project was time-consuming but preferable to a final.

Dr. Fu provided clear lecture materials, that made homeworks a breeze. Homeworks are 40% of the grade, and we had 2-3 a week, but each was only 3-4 questions. Coding these will be helpful, as it can be recycled on 2 take home exams, which closely follow homework and lecture examples. There was no final, only a short FEM project!

Dr. Fu is a great professor who lectures material well and she's very nice. Definitely go to class even though it's not mandatory she may give extra credit. HWs were on Canvas only a few questions some took longer than others. Exams were timed on Canvas but very similar to HWs and class problems. No final exam, a short Abaqus project at the end!

Had him for Heat and Mass Transfer. It's regarded the most difficult ME class, so I can't say my grade was on him. Don't skimp on any of the homeworks, do them well! They will help prepare you for the exam. He does not post lecture notes or make practice exams. Lectures were kinda boring and monotone, but that is more the material than him.

He taught the first half of ME 4124  The lecture was so boring, he basically read trhough ppt.  The midterm was brutal with average of 45 ish. I suggest you avoid him by switching to automotive or robotic.
He's a really nice guy, very easy class. He doesn't like cheaters.
Extremely easy, super nice and friendly, hates cheaters, wants us all to succeed and wants to help.
Katz is a great professor. Tried to be funny in lectures although most of the time it is guest speakers in 2804. Class is really easy, just show up and you'll get an A.
Transportation can be complicated but he gives you plenty of help with homework and exams that with minimal effort you can easily get a high A in the class.

Katz is a fun and enthusiastic professor. 2804 is a busy work class so don't sweat it. Lectures are long and boring, and the "small group" recitation meetings are massive time wasters so just power through and do the writing assignments early.
Great teacher

Dr. Katz is very passionate about what he teaches and is an amazing resource for all things Civil Engineering. His class is entirely lecture based and exploratory. He brings in interesting speakers so the lectures were interesting and engaging.
Lectures not required. Papers every 1-2 weeks. Easy grading. Overall easy but informative class.

Overall a good professor but has boring lectures. Papers and memos due weekly over the last couple of months. Attendance is taken in class each day and he offers extra credit at the end of the semester which can boost your grade by about 3 points. Easy class if you do not procrastinate.

Fluid Dynamics was not easy. Select lectures were posted online so you had to go to class to get the notes. The homework was not bad, and the tests resembled processes used during the homework, the tests are still hard. He says he won't curve but if you show up, do the homework, and talk to him he will help you if you need help.

Took fluids with Dr. Qiao. He is a great, old school professor with vast knowledge of the subject. He gave great lectures, but did not post most of them online so you have to go to class to learn the material. Usually had one hw assignment per week with problems from the textbook. Exams were challenging, but doable if you could do the hw
I took Qiao's class for Fluids. He is good lecturer who makes complex topics funny and interesting.

I felt that the lectures and homeworks did not adequately prepare me for the heavily weighted tests. The conceptual part of the exams and graphing were barely covered, so most of the class lost many points on the tests. It is nice that homework is a completion grade and the workshops ended up being extra credit, but I would not take him again.

This was Binoy's modern binary exploitation class. The class is basically completing RET2's WarGames platform, with lectures from Binoy and his postdocs. Quite frankly, it was pretty easy, but time consuming to complete all problems. Grading was pretty easy bc he offers a lot of partial credit plus he curved at the end (honestly was not needed).

I like the fact that prof. yanardag was very approachable, and she would often check on us about our class project and give feedback.  Her review lectures before exams was very useful, and she gave tons of of hints about what she is gonna ask. Wouldn't recommend if you want an easy A though, homeworks were brutal lol

This was a tough course but I ended up investing a good chunk of my semester into this and learned a lot —she was very accommodating though, she turned the final exam into a take home after seeing us burned out!

It was my first Computer Vision course, and Dr. Yanardag was excellent at explaining concepts with real world examples! The assignments were heavy but I learned a lot (started from Pytorch basics all the way to coding a GAN). Definitely recommend this course if you want to learn deep learning and computer vision.
was ok but wouldn't take again

Genuinely learned a lot from Professor Pinar! She explains concepts clearly and always makes time for questions during her lectures. The projects in this course taught me the skills needed to excel in computer vision. If you put in the effort, you'll see excellent results. Highly recommend taking her class!
Assignments and projects were very helpful in applying what we learned in class. Was very accommodating.
It's good for us to work on the project and provide feedback.
Great course for tip-toeing in real world cases with ML
learned nothing and got nothing out of this

I had him for the second half of CEE 2834 and I have never seen a professor care less about his job than him lol. Always late to class and not helpful, shockingly boring but his expectations were reasonable and his class was not too hard.

Dr. Dogan was a great professor! Though, this class was busy work. There are a lot of group projects and some of my group members were lazy (though there was peer review). If you have the option to, take ENGE 1414. However, Dr. Dogan was an amazing instructor and answered emails fast and truly cared about her students.
Peofessor Hulya Dogan is a great Professor. She is clear and supportive and helpful.

This engineering elective is pretty easy, and I will say Professor Dogan is very nice and helpful when it comes to getting your assignments graded. If you want to redo an assignment, she may allow you to do it! Her class in general isn't hard as long as your team does their part.

Prof. Charles is very knowledgeable about SQL. This is an easy 1-credit class that gives you a good introduction to writing "good" SQL queries. There are 4-5 assignments in the course and the final is a just a final assignment. Highly recommend the class and professor.

Teaches SQL for 2304 - easy class for a 1-hr credit. There's around 4/5 assignments in the class - with the final being more of an assignment, than a test. Make sure to go to class even if its an 8AM, Charles has pretty good lectures and might give out extra credit sometimes. Would recommend if you're interested in learning SQL

I took 2304 for SQL. Prof. Charles is really knowledgeable about SQL and often supplements his lectures with personal stories. He does insist on writing "good SQL", so you need to attend class to learn what his requirements are (StackOverflow has plenty of "bad SQL", so beware). He writes his queries live so you can write yours live with him

Dr. Schroeder is one of my favorite professors at VT. I am not sure if he will be teaching undergrad again but if he does, I cannot recommend him enough. He was incredibly busy this semester yet still took the time to properly walk through the material and was approachable to students. I thoroughly enjoyed his lectures, which is a new first for me

While Kampania was a kind and intelligent professor, a lot of his lecture material wasn't easily applied to the homework and exams (which were all take-home and took a very long time). This is essentially a MATLAB/Mathematica course. All of the homework was virtually impossible without software. Amir is a fantastic and kind TA, I recommend his OHs.

This is not a hard class (or at least it shouldn't be). But watching pre-recorded videos from 4 years ago sucks. This is almost like a flipped class which don't work for some people. All homework requires the use of Matlab or Mathematica. If you don't know Mathematica, good luck because there's no lecture for that.

He is a very knowledgeable professor who makes you work hard so that you can learn deeply about the course matter. Encourages questions in the class and sometimes even read your mind before you even utter a word
Read a textbook instead of taking his class.

Great professor, and not too difficult course material. The quizzes were not too hard and the final exam was very similar in structure to the quizzes, which made it relatively easy to prepare for. Students had the option to attend lectures virtually or in person, and the flexibility was nice.

Pretty good lecturer. Had reasonable expectations for a class that is usually taken alongside the senior capstone project. Class is a semester-long group project focused on learning about agile development. Grading was not harsh and quizzes and tests were relatively easy.

Jaworski is a good guy and professor. He was always respectful and kind. However, the course was very difficult. While Jaworski was excellent at explaining theory, very few examples were given in class, making the homework and exams difficult. The group project, homework, and exams made by the incompetent TAs were consistently terrible.

This was Dr. Denby's first time teaching, and he did an okay job explaining the material. He's knowledgeable but moved quickly on coding and slower on derivations. Dr. Young did a decent job explaining the material and was open to student questions. Class consists of weekly 5-minute short-answer quizzes, biweekly HW, two midterms, and a final. Homework takes time, and exams are open-note and fair but time-consuming. Understand in-class examples and homework problems with posted solutions to prepare for exams.

This is the most chill AOE class on sustainable aviation. All assignments are group-based, including homework, presentations, and reports. The workload isn't difficult or very time-consuming, and there are no exams, which is a nice perk. Definitely take this class it's interesting and not too stressful for a high level technical elective.

Dr.Back is one of the smartest professors I have seen at VT. He is super active on the class website and help channel. As a student, I have gained a lot of knowledge by taking this class.

Though he can sometimes come off as stern, Dr. Back is one of the smartest and hardest-working professors I've ever met. He is extremely active on the class help forums, and the live demos he sprinkles into his lectures are enchanting displays of pure skill. (Ever wanted to watch an rlogin node get overloaded?)
Very snarky. Will find you a discussion thread for a question instead of answering a yes or no. Most outdated and irrelevant course material that is made unnecessarily hard for no reason.

Dr. Back is very knowledgeable about computer systems, so as someone who finds this topic interesting, I really enjoyed his class. Super knowledgeable and engaging lecturer. Has the same general sarcastic/sassy CS professor attitude which can come off as condescending for some. Super active in class forums and discord. This professor is a little bit smarter than the other professors in the CS department but unfortunately his personality is horrible. He's ego is through the roof and he hates looking at other views. He is the reason this class is so impractical.

I took Williams for Systems but I'm going to rate Back as the class assignments are the same among all professors. Definitely the hardest CS class here but the most useful I've taken. Projects and exercises are hard but if you go to the TAs, they will help. You will struggle (cush/threadpool is a pain) but try to work as much as possible.

Grades are returned extremely slowly. Classes end next week and I have no idea if I'm passing or failing. Dr Back is very knowledgeable about his topic; often explains complex topics in, well, a complicated manner. He is good at dumbing stuff down if you ask him one-on-one. Very respectful guy, would take his class again. Systems is difficult so make sure you have a good partner for your projects, and go to office hours often! There's no shame to it :)

The issue isn't the professor, it's the class. Computer Systems is definitely one the hardest classes a CS major will ever take. The material isn't that difficult to understand, it's just the homework (exercises and projects) are just so much work. Just start early on everything and you're good. Dr. Back is a good prof and he posts lecture videos

Dr. Back is really knowledgeable and helpful. He designs almost all of the course material, so he is insanely familiar with the topics. He makes fun of students when they ask questions he thinks are dumb. He does this on public forums which is humiliating. Excellent professor and very helpful.

Back is incredibly arrogant and mean spirited and his lecturing skills are non-existent. His courses are basically impossible and at the end you feel like you know less than you did when you started the course. The only positive things about Back is that he is insanely knowledgeable and easily accessible.
Great Professor!  Very helpful!

3204 is the notorious class for the CS dept at VT.  Back does a good job of presenting the material in the form of slides.
